extraction_notes.note: Algorithm 1 (the analysed blockwise hard-EM operator) is typeset inside a figure with bold headings, not an algorithm environment; extracted as a prose algorithm node with unmarked steps (Initialize, loop with E-step and M-step children, Output). The finishing step warns that it starts at markup.

Lemma 12's quantitative bounds (eqs. 20-24) are derived in running text after the proof environment closes; extracted as a separate prose proof node (continuation) with a proves edge to the lemma and a uses edge to the first proof part.

Lemmas 3 and 15 are textbook facts (predictability of post-stopping-time indicators; gradient inequality for strongly concave functions) stated without citation; marked origin external, standard (uncited), with their proofs kept as paper.

These results are stated without any proof or argument in the paper; given rigor semi_formal. Theorem 5.1, Proposition 4 and Corollary 1 also lack proofs but are condensed main-text versions of Theorem 13.1, Proposition 7 and Corollary 2, so they get uses edges from those instead.

Interpretive paragraphs, the simulation and Oklahoma application results (tables, figures, bootstrap summaries) and the SEM configuration table were not extracted; only the model specifications from those sections became definition nodes.
Section headings carry no printed numbers in the prepared source (the supplement resets counters), so section fields hold titles only.

The standard approximate intervals based on maximum likelihood theory, θ̂ ± σ̂z(α), can be quite misleading. nodes.name: Observed spatiotemporal point pattern and observation window
nodes.statement: We observe a spatiotemporal point pattern \(N\) on \(D_{\rm obs}=[0,T]\times\mathcal S\subset [0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^d\) (typically \(d=2\)).

nodes.name: Base product measure and volume
nodes.statement: We write the base product measure as \(\mathrm{d}\tau=\mathrm{d} t\otimes\mathrm{d}\mu(x)\) and set \(|B|:=\int_B \mathrm{d}\tau\).

nodes.name: Treatment time and post-treatment analysis window
nodes.statement: Treatment is applied at time \(t^\ast\in(0,T]\), and the post-treatment analysis window is \(D=(t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\).

nodes.name: Latent control and treatment components
nodes.statement: On \(D\), the observed process is represented as the superposition of two simple latent component processes, a control component \(N_0\) and a treatment component \(N_1\), so that \(N=N_0+N_1\) and \(N(B)=N_0(B)+N_1(B)\) for every Borel set \(B\subseteq D\).
nodes.statement_short: On the post-treatment window the observed process is the superposition N = N_0 + N_1 of latent control and treatment components.

nodes.name: Exogenous finite tessellation
nodes.statement: The tessellation $\mathcal T=\{\mathcal I_j\}_{j=1}^J$ is a finite, time-invariant partition of $(t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S$: there exists a finite partition $\{\mathcal S_j\}_{j=1}^J$ of $\mathcal S$ such that \[ \mathcal I_j := (t^\ast,T]\times \mathcal S_j,\qquad j=1,\ldots,J, \] with $|\mathcal I_j|>0$ for all $j$. Moreover, there exists a $\sigma$-field $\mathscr T$ such that $\mathcal T$ is $\mathscr T$-measurable and $\mathscr T$ is independent of $\sigma(N)$. If $\mathcal T$ is deterministic, the exogeneity condition is vacuous.
nodes.label: ass:tessellation

nodes.name: Binary treatment vector
nodes.statement: Let $Z$ denote the binary treatment vector, and $Z_j$ the treatment status of $\mathcal{I}_j$.

nodes.name: Realised treatment vector vs fixed allocation
nodes.statement: Throughout, \(Z\in\{0,1\}^J\) denotes the realised random treatment vector, while \(z\in\{0,1\}^J\) denotes a fixed allocation value used in an intervention.

nodes.name: Discrete-time period counts
nodes.statement: Fix a tessellation \(\mathcal T=\{\mathcal I_j\}_{j=1}^J\) satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:tessellation}, with \(\mathcal I_j=(t^\ast,T]\times \mathcal S_j\). For intuition only, choose grid points \(t^\ast=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_M=T\), and define the period counts \( Y_j^m:=N((s_{m-1},s_m]\times \mathcal S_j), \qquad j=1,\ldots,J,\ \ m=1,\ldots,M. \)
nodes.statement_short: For intuition, period counts Y_j^m count events of cell j in the m-th time period of a grid.

nodes.name: do-intervention notation
nodes.statement: Using Pearl's intervention notation, $\mathrm{do}(Z=z)$ denotes the hypothetical intervention that sets the treatment allocation to $z$, rather than conditioning on the event $Z=z$ in the observed data-generating process \citep{pearl2009causal}.

nodes.name: Potential process and potential cell/total counts
nodes.statement: For a fixed allocation \(z\in\{0,1\}^J\), let \(N^z\) denote the post-treatment potential process on \(D\) under the intervention \(\mathrm{do}(Z=z)\), and define the cell-level and total post-treatment counts \[ Y_j(z):=N^z(\mathcal I_j),\qquad Y_\bullet(z):=N^z(D)=\sum_{j=1}^J Y_j(z). \]
nodes.statement_short: N^z is the post-treatment potential process under do(Z=z); Y_j(z) and Y_•(z) are its cell and total counts.
also_stated_at: For each \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\), let \(N^z\) denote the post-treatment potential point process that would be observed on \((t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\) under the intervention \(\mathrm{do}(Z=z)\), and define the corresponding cell counts \(Y_j(z):=N^z(\mathcal I_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).

nodes.name: Coordinate-switched allocations
nodes.statement: For a reference allocation \(z\), let \(z^{j=1}\) and \(z^{j=0}\) denote the allocations obtained by setting the \(j\)th coordinate of \(z\) to \(1\) and \(0\), respectively, while leaving all other coordinates unchanged.

nodes.name: Individual Treatment Effect (ITE)
nodes.statement: For cell \(\mathcal I_j\), define \[ \psi_j(z) := \mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_j\!\left(z^{j=1}\right)\right] - \mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_j\!\left(z^{j=0}\right)\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^{z^{j=1}}(\mathcal I_j)\right] - \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^{z^{j=0}}(\mathcal I_j)\right]. \]
nodes.statement_short: psi_j(z): difference in expected cell-j counts when cell j is switched to treated vs untreated, other cells fixed at z.

nodes.name: Average Individual Treatment Effect (AITE)
nodes.statement: \[ \psi(z):=\frac{1}{J}\sum_{j=1}^J \psi_j(z). \]

nodes.name: Difference under fixed allocations (DAITE)
nodes.statement: For \(z_a,z_b\in\{0,1\}^J\), define \[ \psi(z_a,z_b) := \mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_\bullet(z_a)\right] - \mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_\bullet(z_b)\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^{z_a}(D)\right] - \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^{z_b}(D)\right]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Difference in expected total post-treatment counts between two fixed allocations z_a and z_b.

nodes.name: Treatment AITE (TAITE) and DTAITE
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\{0,1\}^J\) be a finite set of allocations. Define \[ \psi(\mathcal Z):=\frac{1}{|\mathcal Z|}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\psi(z). \] For two finite sets \(\mathcal Z_a,\mathcal Z_b\subseteq\{0,1\}^J\), define \( \psi(\mathcal Z_a,\mathcal Z_b):=\psi(\mathcal Z_a)-\psi(\mathcal Z_b). \) Equivalently, if \(\pi_{\mathcal Z}\) denotes the uniform distribution on \(\mathcal Z\), then \[ \psi(\mathcal Z)=\sum_{z}\pi_{\mathcal Z}(z)\psi(z), \qquad \psi(\mathcal Z_a,\mathcal Z_b) = \sum_z \pi_{\mathcal Z_a}(z)\psi(z) - \sum_z \pi_{\mathcal Z_b}(z)\psi(z). \]
nodes.statement_short: TAITE averages the AITE over a finite allocation set; DTAITE is the difference of two TAITEs.

nodes.name: Observed filtration
nodes.statement: We model the observed process \(N\) as a simple counting measure on \(D\), adapted to the observed filtration \((\mathcal H_t)_{t\in[t^\ast,T]}\).

nodes.name: Borel sigma-algebra on D
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal B(D)\) denote the Borel \(\sigma\)-algebra on \(D\).

nodes.name: Conditional intensity
nodes.statement: Whenever the \(\mathcal H\)-conditional intensity exists, it is the predictable process \[ \lambda(\tau;\theta\mid\mathcal H_{t-}) =\lim_{(h,\delta)\downarrow 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}\big[N([t,t+h)\times B_\delta(x))\mid\mathcal H_{t-}\big]} {h\,\mu(B_\delta(x))}, \qquad \tau=(t,x)\in D, \] where \(B_r(x)\) denotes the Euclidean ball of radius \(r\) centred at \(x\).
nodes.statement_short: The H-conditional intensity is the limit of expected counts in small space-time neighbourhoods per unit time and area.

nodes.name: Component intensities
nodes.statement: When we later work with the latent component processes \(N_0\) and \(N_1\), we write \(\lambda_0\) and \(\lambda_1\) for the corresponding component intensities under the filtration then in force, with \(\lambda=\lambda_0+\lambda_1\).

nodes.name: Simple point process
nodes.statement: A point process is {\sl simple} if, with probability one, all points are distinct.
differentia: with probability one, all points are distinct

nodes.name: Conditional intensity determines the law of a simple point process
nodes.statement: Since the conditional intensity \(\lambda\) uniquely determines the finite-dimensional distributions of a simple point process (Proposition 7.2.IV of \citet{daley2003introduction}), one typically specifies a simple spatiotemporal point process through a model for \(\lambda\).
conclusions: the conditional intensity \(\lambda\) uniquely determines the finite-dimensional distributions of a simple point process

nodes.name: Stationary point process
nodes.statement: A point process is {\sl stationary} if its law is invariant under shifts in time and/or space (e.g.\ Definition 12.1.II of \citet{daley2007introduction}).
differentia: its law is invariant under shifts in time and/or space

nodes.name: Hawkes process
nodes.statement: A canonical history dependent specification is the Hawkes process \citep{Hawkes1,hawkes1974cluster}, the conditional intensity of which takes the form \begin{equation} \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal H_{t-};\theta) = \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\int_{(t-h,t)\times B_R(x)} g_{k\ell}(t-u,x-y;\theta) N_\ell(\mathrm{d} u,\mathrm{d} y) \end{equation} where \(\mu_k(\tau;\theta)\ge 0\) are background intensities, \(g_{k\ell}\ge 0\) are triggering kernels with finite support \((0,h]\times B_R(0)\), and \(N_\ell\) denotes the component counting measure.
nodes.statement_short: Hawkes process: intensity = background mu_k plus finite-support triggering kernels g_kl integrated against past component events.

nodes.name: Canonical bivariate Hawkes intensity
nodes.statement: \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal H_{t-};\theta) = \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\int_{(t-h,t)\times B_R(x)} g_{k\ell}(t-u,x-y;\theta) N_\ell(\mathrm{d} u,\mathrm{d} y)
nodes.label: eq:canonicalHawkes

nodes.name: Covariate field
nodes.statement: We allow the treatment and control intensities to depend on an observed predictable covariate field \(\mathbf{X}(\tau)\in\mathbb R^p\) (e.g., spatial inhomogeneity, seasonality, weather, or population density), writing \( \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal H_{t-};\theta) = \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal H_{t-},\mathbf{X};\theta). \)

nodes.name: Target allocation set
nodes.statement: Let \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\subseteq \{0,1\}^J\) denote the set of treatment allocations relevant to the scientific question (or, more generally, the support of the policies under comparison).

nodes.name: Potential latent components
nodes.statement: Under \(\mathrm{do}(Z=z)\), the post-treatment process remains a superposition \( N^z=N_0^z+N_1^z, \) and the allocation field \(z\) may affect both component intensities through the post-treatment dynamics.

nodes.name: Pre-intervention information
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, define the pre-intervention information \( \mathcal B_0:=\sigma(\mathcal T,\mathbf{X})\vee \mathcal H_{t^\ast-}, \) that is, the \(\sigma\)-field generated by the tessellation, the exogenous covariate path, and the observed history up to \(t^\ast\).

nodes.name: Well-defined interventions and consistency
nodes.statement: For every \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\), the intervention \(\mathrm{do}(Z=z)\) defines a unique post-treatment potential process \(N^z\). Moreover, if the realised treatment vector equals \(z\), then \[ N(B)=N^z(B)\qquad\text{a.s. for every Borel }B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S. \] The pre-treatment history \(\mathcal H_{t^\ast-}\), the tessellation \(\mathcal T\), and the exogenous covariate path \(\mathbf{X}\) are common across \(\{N^z:z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\}\).
nodes.label: ass:id-consistency

nodes.name: Conditional exchangeability
nodes.statement: \[ \{N^z:z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\}\ \perp\!\!\!\perp\ Z\ \big|\ \mathcal B_0. \] That is, after conditioning on \(\mathcal B_0\), the realised treatment allocation carries no additional information about the collection of potential post-treatment processes.
nodes.label: ass:id-exchange

nodes.name: Positivity on the design support
nodes.statement: There exists a subset \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\subseteq \mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\), \( \mathbb{P}(Z=z\mid \mathcal B_0)>0\qquad\text{a.s.} \) If the target of interest is a randomised policy \(\pi\) over allocations, it suffices that \(\mathrm{supp}(\pi)\subseteq \mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\).
nodes.label: ass:id-positivity

nodes.name: Identification on the observed design support
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:id-consistency}--\ref{ass:id-positivity} hold. Then for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\), \( \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^z(B)\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}\!\left\{N(B)\mid Z=z,\mathcal B_0\right\}\right]. \) Equivalently, for each cell \(\mathcal I_j\), \( \mathbb{E}\!\left[Y_j(z)\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbb{E}\!\left\{N(\mathcal I_j)\mid Z=z,\mathcal B_0\right\}\right]. \)
nodes.statement_short: Point-process g-formula: on the design support, interventional expected counts equal averaged conditional observed counts.
nodes.label: prop:id-onsupport

nodes.name: Interventional mean measure
nodes.statement: For a point process, the natural mean object under allocation \(z\) is the map \[ B \mapsto \mathbb{E}[N^z(B)], \] which gives the expected number of post-treatment events falling in any Borel region \(B \subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\). We refer to this expected-count map as the interventional mean measure.

nodes.name: Potential post-treatment filtration
nodes.statement: To formalise this, let \[ \mathcal F_t^z := \sigma\!\Big( \mathcal B_0,\, N^z\big((t^\ast,s]\times A\big):s\le t,\ A\in\mathcal B(\mathcal S) \Big), \qquad t\in[t^\ast,T], \] be the filtration generated by \(\mathcal B_0\) and the post-treatment potential history under allocation \(z\).

nodes.name: Common structural model across regimes
nodes.statement: There exists \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) such that, for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\), the potential process \(N^z\) admits latent component processes \((N_0^z,N_1^z)\) with \( N^z=N_0^z+N_1^z, \) and predictable component intensities \( \lambda_{k,\theta^\star}^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X})\) for \( k\in\{0,1\}, \) so that the total intensity is \[ \lambda_{\theta^\star}^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X}) = \lambda_{0,\theta^\star}^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X}) + \lambda_{1,\theta^\star}^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X}). \] Equivalently, the family \(\{N^z:z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\}\) is generated by a common parametric model \(\{\lambda_\theta^z:\theta\in\Theta\}\), with the same true parameter value \(\theta^\star\) across all regimes \(z\). Under the observed allocation \(Z\), the observed post-treatment process is generated by the corresponding regime \(z=Z\).
nodes.label: ass:id-structural

nodes.name: Identifiability of the structural parameter
nodes.statement: If \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta\) satisfy \[ \mathcal L_\theta\!\left(N\mid Z=z,\mathcal B_0\right) = \mathcal L_{\theta'}\!\left(N\mid Z=z,\mathcal B_0\right) \qquad\text{a.s. for every } z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}, \] then \(\theta=\theta'\).
nodes.label: ass:id-theta

nodes.name: Model-based interventional mean measure
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{ass:id-structural}, each regime \(z\) induces an interventional mean measure \begin{equation} \Lambda_\theta^z(B\mid \mathcal B_0) := \mathbb{E}_\theta\!\left[ \int_B \lambda_\theta^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X})\,\mathrm{d}\tau \,\Big|\, \mathcal B_0 \right], \qquad B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Interventional mean measure under the structural model
nodes.statement: \Lambda_\theta^z(B\mid \mathcal B_0) := \mathbb{E}_\theta\!\left[ \int_B \lambda_\theta^z(\tau\mid \mathcal F_{t-}^z,\mathbf{X})\,\mathrm{d}\tau \,\Big|\, \mathcal B_0 \right], \qquad B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S.
nodes.label: eq:id-mean-measure

nodes.name: Model-based identification of off-support regimes
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:id-consistency}, \ref{ass:id-exchange}, \ref{ass:id-structural}, and \ref{ass:id-theta} hold, and that \(\theta^\star\) is identified from the observed law on \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\). Then for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}}\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\), \[ \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^z(B)\mid \mathcal B_0\right] = \Lambda_{\theta^\star}^z(B\mid \mathcal B_0), \qquad \mathbb{E}\!\left[N^z(B)\right] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\Lambda_{\theta^\star}^z(B\mid \mathcal B_0)\right]. \] Hence every causal estimand in \cref{sec:causalEstimands} that can be written as a finite linear combination of \(\{\mathbb{E}[N^z(B)]: z\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{tar}},\ B\subseteq (t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S\}\) is identified by \(\theta^\star\).
assumptions: that \(\theta^\star\) is identified from the observed law on \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{supp}}\)
conclusions: Hence every causal estimand in \cref{sec:causalEstimands} that can be written as a finite linear combination
nodes.statement_short: Under a regime-stable structural model with identified theta*, all interventional mean measures (and causal estimands) are identified.
nodes.label: prop:id-offsupport

nodes.name: Latent event labels vs cell treatment
nodes.statement: The treatment vector \(Z\) (or fixed allocation \(z\)) specifies the intervention regime for cells, whereas the latent variable \(r_i\in\{0,1\}\) records which component process generated event \(\gamma_i\).

nodes.name: Latent labelling
nodes.statement: Post-treatment, the observed process \(N=N_0+N_1\) is unlabelled; let \(r=(r_i)_{i=1}^{N(D)}\in\{0,1\}^{N(D)}\) be the latent labels of events \(\gamma_i\).

nodes.name: Label-induced component intensities
nodes.statement: Given a candidate labelling \(r\), let \(\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\) denote the component intensities obtained by feeding only past labels \(r_{1:N(t-)}\) into the predictable integrands.

nodes.name: Complete-data maximiser
nodes.statement: The complete-data maximiser \begin{equation} \tilde\theta_r:=\arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta}\ell_r(\theta) \end{equation} is well defined under standard regularity \citep{ogata1978asymptotic,RATHBUN199655}.

nodes.name: Complete-data maximiser
nodes.statement: \tilde\theta_r:=\arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta}\ell_r(\theta)
nodes.label: eq:cdll-main

nodes.name: Observed-data likelihood
nodes.statement: The complete-data log-likelihood \eqref{eq:cdll-main} induces the marginal (observed-data) likelihood \begin{equation} L(\theta)\equiv p(N\mid \theta) =\sum_{r\in\{0,1\}^{N(D)}} p(N,r\mid \theta) =\sum_{r}\exp\{\ell_r(\theta)\}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Observed-data likelihood as sum over labellings
nodes.statement: L(\theta)\equiv p(N\mid \theta) =\sum_{r\in\{0,1\}^{N(D)}} p(N,r\mid \theta) =\sum_{r}\exp\{\ell_r(\theta)\}.
nodes.label: eq:obsLike

nodes.name: EM algorithm
nodes.statement: A standard EM algorithm to compute maximum likelihood estimates in this context iterates between expectation and maximisation steps as follows: the expectation step given current parameter vector $\theta'$ can be computed as \begin{align} Q(\theta,\theta') = \mathbb{E}_{r \mid N, \theta'}\!\left[ \log p(N,r \mid \theta)\right] = \sum_{r} \log p(N,r \mid \theta)\, p(r \mid N, \theta') \end{align} where the expectation is with respect to the conditional distribution of the labels $r$ given the observed data $N$ under parameter value $\theta'$. Next the maximisation step is defined via the updated estimate \( \hat\theta = \arg\max_\theta Q(\theta,\theta'). \)
nodes.statement_short: Standard EM: compute the expected complete-data log-likelihood Q under the label posterior, then maximise it over theta.

nodes.name: EM Q-function
nodes.statement: Q(\theta,\theta') = \mathbb{E}_{r \mid N, \theta'}\!\left[ \log p(N,r \mid \theta)\right] = \sum_{r} \log p(N,r \mid \theta)\, p(r \mid N, \theta')
nodes.label: eq:Q

nodes.name: Monte Carlo E-step objective
nodes.statement: Conceptually, if exact draws from \(p(r\mid N,\theta')\) were available, we would approximate the E-step by \begin{equation} Q^*(\theta,\theta') = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M \log p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta), \end{equation} where $\{r^{(i)}\colon i =1,\ldots,M\}$ is a random sample from $p(r \mid N, \theta')$.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo approximation Q*
nodes.statement: Q^*(\theta,\theta') = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M \log p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta),
nodes.label: eq:Qstar

nodes.name: Proposal distribution over labellings
nodes.statement: In our setting, we cannot sample directly from \(p(r\mid N,\theta')\), so we introduce a proposal distribution \(q(r\mid N)\) from which sampling is easy.

nodes.name: Importance-weighted EM objective
nodes.statement: Draw \(r^{(1)},\ldots,r^{(M)}\) independently from \(q(r\mid N)\). We then approximate the EM objective by \begin{equation} Q^\dagger(\theta,\theta') = \sum_{i=1}^M w_i \log p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta), \end{equation} where \begin{align} w_i \propto \frac{p(r^{(i)}\mid N,\theta')}{q(r^{(i)}\mid N)} \propto \frac{p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta')}{q(r^{(i)}\mid N)}, \end{align} and the constant of proportionality is chosen so that \(\sum_{i=1}^M w_i=1\).
nodes.statement_short: Importance-sampled EM objective: weighted average of complete-data log-likelihoods of labellings drawn from proposal q.

nodes.name: Importance-weighted objective Q-dagger
nodes.statement: Q^\dagger(\theta,\theta') = \sum_{i=1}^M w_i \log p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta),
nodes.label: eq:Qdagger

nodes.name: Importance weights
nodes.statement: w_i \propto \frac{p(r^{(i)}\mid N,\theta')}{q(r^{(i)}\mid N)} \propto \frac{p(N,r^{(i)}\mid \theta')}{q(r^{(i)}\mid N)},
nodes.label: eq:w

nodes.name: Deterministic update schedule and blocks
nodes.statement: Fix the deterministic update schedule \( t^\ast=u_0<u_1<\cdots<u_{\mathfrak{T}}=T\), \( D_m:=(u_{m-1},u_m]\times\mathcal S\), \( D^{(m)}:=(t^\ast,u_m]\times\mathcal S. \)

nodes.name: Hard-EM label and parameter iterates
nodes.statement: After the first \(m\) blocks have been processed, the hard-EM proof device has produced a label vector \(r^{(m)}\) for the events in \(D^{(m)}\) and a parameter iterate \(\theta^{(m)}\).

nodes.name: True labelling
nodes.statement: Let \(r^\star\) denote the true latent post-treatment labelling.

nodes.name: Restricted Hamming distance and prefix mislabelling rate
nodes.statement: The restricted Hamming distance \[ d_H^{[u_m]}(r^{(m)},r^\star) = \sum_{i:\,t_i\le u_m}\mathbbm{1}\{r_i^{(m)}\neq r_i^\star\} \] counts label errors among events observed up to time \(u_m\), and the corresponding prefix mislabelling rate is \[ e_m:=\frac{d_H^{[u_m]}(r^{(m)},r^\star)}{|D^{(m)}|}, \qquad e_0:=0. \]

nodes.name: Prefix fraction omega_m
nodes.statement: We also write \[ \omega_m:=\frac{|D^{(m)}|}{|D^{(m+1)}|}, \] so \(\omega_m\) is the fraction of the next prefix window coming from already-processed blocks.

nodes.name: Oracle LLR, decisive sets and ambiguous band
nodes.statement: Define the oracle log-likelihood ratio \[ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)=\log\frac{\lambda_1^\star(\tau)}{\lambda_0^\star(\tau)}, \] the decisive sets \( S_{\theta^\star}^+(b):=\{\tau:\ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)\ge b\}\), \( S_{\theta^\star}^-(b):=\{\tau:\ s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)\le -b\}, \) and the ambiguous band \( A_{\theta^\star}(2b):=\{\tau:\ |s^{\rm or}_{\theta^\star}(\tau)|\le 2b\}. \)
nodes.statement_short: Oracle log intensity ratio s^or; decisive sets where |s^or| >= b with fixed sign; ambiguous band where |s^or| <= 2b.

nodes.name: Blockwise floor term
nodes.statement: The blockwise floor term is \[ \varepsilon_{b,m} := \eta_+\bigl(|D_{m+1}|;b\bigr) + \eta_-\bigl(|D_{m+1}|;b\bigr) + \frac{2}{|D_{m+1}|}\, N\!\big(A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\cap D_{m+1}\big), \] where \(\eta_\pm(\cdot;b)\) are the small oracle-minority rates from Assumption~\ref{ass:G8}.

nodes.name: E-step and M-step fluctuation terms
nodes.statement: The E-step and M-step fluctuation terms are \[ \delta_m := C_{\rm H,1}\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}{|D_{m+1}|}}, \qquad \xi_m := \frac{C_{\rm sc}}{m_{\rm sc}} \left( \sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}{|D^{(m)}|}} + \frac{z_{\rm Fr}}{|D^{(m)}|} \right), \] where \(K_{\rm win}\) is the window-envelope constant from Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime}, \(z_{\rm Fr}\) is the Freedman inequality/union-bound level from the Supplement, and \(m_{\rm sc}\) is the local strong-concavity modulus from Assumption~\ref{ass:G6}.

nodes.name: Contraction to a statistical floor
nodes.statement: Assume that Assumptions~\ref{ass:G0},~\ref{ass:G0pred},~\ref{ass:G1}--\ref{ass:G9}, and~\ref{ass:warmstart} hold, and choose \(b\) and \(\alpha\) so that the sufficient condition \eqref{eq:EsufficientB} holds. In particular, on each newly processed block the greedy E-step assigns no minority labels on decisive regions relative to the current iterate \(\theta^{(m)}\). Let \[ A:=\frac{L_s}{b}, \] where \(L_s\) is the LLR Lipschitz constant from Assumption~\ref{ass:G5}. Then, on the same high-probability event as \cref{thm:contract}, there exists a constant \(B_{\rm main}>0\) (the M-step sensitivity constant derived in the Supplement) such that, for every block \(m\), \[ e_{m+1} \le \omega_m e_m + (1-\omega_m)\Big(A\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|+\varepsilon_{b,m}+\delta_m\Big), \] and \( \|\theta^{(m+1)}-\theta^\star\| \le B_{\rm main}\,e_{m+1}+\xi_{m+1}. \) If \(\omega:=\max_m\omega_m<1\) and \( \rho:=\omega+(1-\omega)AB_{\rm main}<1, \) then the label error decays geometrically up to a floor of order \[ \frac{1}{1-\rho}\max_m\big(\varepsilon_{b,m}+\delta_m+A\xi_m\big), \] and the parameter error decays geometrically up to the induced floor \[ B_{\rm main}\frac{1}{1-\rho}\max_m\big(\varepsilon_{b,m}+\delta_m+A\xi_m\big)+\max_m\xi_m. \]
assumptions: choose \(b\) and \(\alpha\) so that the sufficient condition \eqref{eq:EsufficientB} holds
conclusions: then the label error decays geometrically up to a floor of order
and the parameter error decays geometrically up to the induced floor
nodes.statement_short: Blockwise hard-EM label error and parameter error obey a two-line recursion and contract geometrically to a statistical floor.
nodes.label: thm:sec-contraction

nodes.name: Compatibility conditions for consistency
nodes.statement: Let the quantities in \cref{thm:sec-contraction} carry an \(n\)-index, with \(|D_n|\to\infty\). If \( b_n\downarrow 0\), \( \Delta_{s,n}=o(b_n)\), \( L_{s,n}B_{{\rm main},n}=o(b_n), \) and \( \max_m \varepsilon_{b_n,m}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0\), \( \max_m \delta_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0\), \( \max_m \xi_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0\), with \(\sup_n\max_m \omega_{m,n}<1\), then \( \|\theta_n^{(\mathfrak{T}_n)}-\theta_n^\star\|\xrightarrow{\mathbb P} 0. \) For Hawkes models, a sufficient route is that \[ \varepsilon_{{\rm col},n}\log |D_n|=o(b_n), \qquad \frac{L_{s,n}\log|D_n|}{m_{{\rm sc},n}}=o(b_n), \] where \(\varepsilon_{{\rm col},n}\) is the column-similarity error from the Hawkes process alignment verification, together with an array-level vanishing-band condition derived from \cref{lem:regA,lem:regB}. Without such array-level scaling, the Hawkes process theory generally gives contraction to a non-zero floor rather than automatic consistency. Note that along the triangular array we allow the true data-generating parameter to vary with \(n\), writing \(\theta_n^\star\). In the fixed-parameter case, \(\theta_n^\star\equiv\theta^\star\).
assumptions: Let the quantities in \cref{thm:sec-contraction} carry an \(n\)-index, with \(|D_n|\to\infty\).
nodes.statement_short: Along a triangular array, vanishing floor and fluctuation terms with b_n balancing alignment and contraction give parameter consistency.
nodes.label: prop:compatibility

nodes.name: Transfer to plug-in causal estimands
nodes.statement: For any finite linear functional \[ F(\theta)=\sum_{\ell=1}^M c_\ell \Lambda_\theta^{z_\ell}(B_\ell), \] on the high-probability event of \cref{thm:sec-contraction}, \[ |F(\theta^{(m)})-F(\theta^\star)| \le L_\lambda\Big(\sum_{\ell=1}^M |c_\ell|\,|B_\ell|\Big)\,\|\theta^{(m)}-\theta^\star\|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Plug-in error of any finite linear functional of interventional mean measures is Lipschitz in the parameter error.
nodes.label: thm:sec-estimands

nodes.name: Consistency of plug-in causal estimands
nodes.statement: Under \cref{prop:compatibility}, plug-in estimators are consistent for fixed-volume causal functionals, including cell-wise contrasts with uniformly bounded cell size and volume-normalised global contrasts. For unnormalised growing-window totals, consistency additionally requires \[ \Big(\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}|c_{\ell,n}|\,|B_{\ell,n}|\Big)\, \|\theta_n^{(\mathfrak{T}_n)}-\theta_n^\star\| \xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0. \]
conclusions: plug-in estimators are consistent for fixed-volume causal functionals, including cell-wise contrasts with uniformly bounded cell size and volume-normalised global contrasts.
For unnormalised growing-window totals, consistency additionally requires
nodes.label: cor:estimands-compat

nodes.name: Simulation model: exponential-Gaussian spatiotemporal Hawkes processes
nodes.statement: We consider two spatiotemporal Hawkes processes, one for control and one for treatment, with exponential temporal decay and Gaussian spatial kernel. For $k\in\{c,t\}$ the conditional intensity is \begin{equation*} \lambda_k(t,x,y \mid \mathcal{H}_{t-}) = \mu_k + K_k \sum_{t_i < t} \exp\!\left\{-\beta_k (t-t_i) - \alpha_k \big\|(x,y) - (x_i,y_i)\big\|_{2}^{2} \right\}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Control and treatment are Hawkes processes with exponential temporal decay and Gaussian spatial kernel.

nodes.name: Spatial interaction scale and cell size
nodes.statement: In space, let \(L_{\text{process}}\) denote the characteristic spatial interaction or decay length of the process and \(L_{\text{cell}}\) a characteristic cell size, for example the square root of the average cell area.

nodes.name: Temporal memory scale
nodes.statement: In time, let \(H_{\text{process}}\) denote the characteristic memory or temporal decay scale of the process, to be compared with the post-treatment analysis horizon \(T-t^\ast\).

nodes.name: Discrepancy-guided relabelling proposal
nodes.statement: Let \(C_j^{\text{obs}}:=N(\mathcal I_j)\) denote the observed post-treatment count in cell \(\mathcal I_j\). Using the current iterate \(\theta'\), compute the component-wise predicted post-treatment counts \[ C_{j,0}:=\int_{\mathcal I_j}\widehat\lambda_0(\tau;\theta')\,\mathrm{d}\tau, \qquad C_{j,1}:=\int_{\mathcal I_j}\widehat\lambda_1(\tau;\theta')\,\mathrm{d}\tau, \] or their simulation-based analogues when these integrals are not available in closed form. Using the current estimates \(\lambda_0(\cdot\mid\theta'_0)\) and \(\lambda_1(\cdot\mid\theta'_1)\), compute predicted post-treatment counts \(C_{j,0}\) and \(C_{j,1}\) (via compensator integrals or fast simulation), and define \[ D_j^{+}=\bigl(C_j^{\text{obs}}-C_{j,0}\bigr)_+, \qquad D_j^{-}=\bigl(C_{j,0}-C_j^{\text{obs}}\bigr)_+. \] Large \(D_j^{+}\) flags excess mass the control model cannot explain and suggests flipping control labels to treatment in \(\mathcal I_j\); \(D_j^{-}\) suggests the reverse. A single proposal is generated by (i) initializing from a baseline labelling \(r_{\text{base}}\) (for example, \(r_i=Z_j\) for each event \(\gamma_i\in\mathcal I_j\)); (ii) drawing flip budgets \(P^{+}\sim\mathrm{Poisson}\!\bigl(\sum_j D_j^{+}\bigr)\) and \(P^{-}\sim\mathrm{Poisson}\!\bigl(\sum_j D_j^{-}\bigr)\); (iii) forming cell weights \(W_j^{+}\propto D_j^{+}\) and \(W_j^{-}\propto D_j^{-}\); (iv) sampling \((L_1^{+},\dots,L_J^{+})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(P^{+};W^{+})\) and \((L_1^{-},\dots,L_J^{-})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(P^{-};W^{-})\); and (v) within each cell \(j\), uniformly relabelling \(L_j^{+}\) currently control-labelled points to treatment and \(L_j^{-}\) currently treatment-labelled points to control.
nodes.statement_short: Proposal for SEM: compare observed and predicted control counts per cell, then randomly flip labels in cells with the largest discrepancies.

nodes.name: Bivariate marked ETAS model for Oklahoma
nodes.statement: Let $z\in\{0,1\}$ index latent process. The conditional intensity for component $k\in\{0,1\}$ takes the form \[ \lambda_k(t,x,y) = \frac{\mu_k}{|S_k|}\, W_k(x,y) + \sum_{\ell \in \{0,1\}} \sum_{\substack{j : t_j < t \\ r_j = \ell}} A_{k\ell}\, e^{\alpha_{m,k\ell}(m_j - m_0)}\, g(t - t_j)\, f(x-x_j, y-y_j \mid m_j), \] with Omori-Utsu $g(\Delta t)=\frac{p-1}{c}(1+\Delta t/c)^{-p}$ on $\Delta t>0$ and power-law spatial factor $f \propto (1+r^2/d(m_j))^{-q}$ with $d(m_j)=D\exp\{\gamma(m_j-m_0)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bivariate ETAS: KDE background plus magnitude-scaled Omori-Utsu temporal and power-law spatial triggering with cross-excitation.

nodes.name: Deterministic partition and prefix windows
nodes.statement: Fix a deterministic partition \begin{align*} t^\ast=&u_0<u_1<\cdots<u_{\mathfrak{T}}=T,\\ D_m:=&(u_{m-1},u_m]\times\mathcal S,\\ D^{[u]}:=(&t^\ast,u]\times\mathcal S,\\ D^{(m)}:=&D^{[u_m]}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Shifted ground counting process
nodes.statement: Throughout the remainder of this section we work on the inference window $D=(t^\ast,T]\times\mathcal S$ and use the shifted ground counting process \[ N^D(t):=N\big((t^\ast,t]\times\mathcal S\big),\qquad t\in[t^\ast,T], \] with the convention $N^D(t^\ast)=0$ (hence also $N^D(t^\ast-)=0$).

nodes.name: Pre-t* history in component-dependent models
nodes.statement: The preceding conditioning convention is sufficient for the model-agnostic setup, but for specializations in which the component intensities depend on component-specific pre-\(t^\ast\) history (notably Hawkes models), conditioning only on the superposed history \(N\) before \(t^\ast\) is not enough to identify the oracle intensities \(\lambda_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)\). In those specializations we therefore work either under empty pre-history or conditional on the marked pre-\(t^\ast\) history \((N_0,N_1)\) over the memory window; see \S\ref{app:hawkes}.
nodes.label: rem:prehistory-marked

nodes.name: Oracle filtration
nodes.statement: The oracle filtration $\{\mathcal G_t\}$ augments $\{\mathcal H_t\}$ with the true component labels $r^\star=(r^\star_i)_{i=1}^{N(D)}$, so that $N_0,N_1$ are adapted to $\{\mathcal G_t\}$.

nodes.name: Model vs observed vs algorithmic objects
nodes.statement: Before proceeding, we note three related objects. (i) Model: the marked process $(N_0,N_1)$, the oracle filtration $(\mathcal G_t)$, and the oracle intensities $\lambda_k(\cdot\mid \mathcal G_{t-};\theta)$. (ii) Observed process: the superposed process $N=N_0+N_1$ and the observed filtration $(\mathcal H_t)$. (iii) Algorithm/analysis: label sequences $r$, induced counts $N_k^r$, and label-induced intensities $\widehat\lambda_k^r(\cdot;\theta)$, which are constructed from $(\mathcal H_t)$ and past labels only (Assumption~\ref{ass:G0pred}).
nodes.label: rem:objects

nodes.name: True oracle intensities
nodes.statement: Write $\lambda_k^\star(\tau):=\lambda_k(\tau\mid \mathcal G_{t-};\theta^\star)$ and $\lambda^\star:=\lambda_0^\star+\lambda_1^\star$.

nodes.name: Compensated martingales
nodes.statement: For any predictable set $S\subset D$, define the component compensated martingales \[ M_k^\star(S)\ :=\ N_k(S) - \int_S \lambda_k^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau,\qquad k\in\{0,1\}, \] and the superposed compensated martingale \[ M^\star(S)\ :=\ N(S) - \int_S \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau\ =\ M_0^\star(S)+M_1^\star(S). \]

nodes.name: Visited labellings
nodes.statement: For the analysed update path $(r^{(m)})_{m=0}^{\mathfrak{T}}$ we denote the (random) set of visited labellings by \[ \mathcal R_{\rm path} :=\big\{r^{(m)}:\ m=0,1,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Single-flip closure of the path
nodes.statement: When single-event perturbations of an iterate labelling are needed (e.g.\ in per-flip arguments), we write the (optional) single-flip closure \[ \mathcal R_{\rm path}^{\rm flip} :=\mathcal R_{\rm path}\ \cup\ \big\{\big(r^{(m)}\big)^{(\gamma_j)}:\ m=0,1,\dots,\mathfrak{T},\ j\le N^{(m)}\big\}, \] where $(r^{(m)})^{(\gamma_j)}$ denotes the labelling obtained by flipping only the $j$th coordinate of $r^{(m)}$ (as in Lemma~\ref{lem:singleflip-nonant}).

nodes.name: Parameter space and constrained set
nodes.statement: Throughout we assume the parameter space $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ is nonempty, and we fix a nonempty, compact and convex subset $\Theta_\circ\subset\Theta$.

nodes.name: M-step maximiser correspondence
nodes.statement: For any nonempty compact convex set $K\subseteq\Theta_\circ$ and any labelling $r$, define \[ \operatorname{ArgMax}_K(r)\ :=\ \arg\max_{\theta\in K}\ell_r(\theta), \qquad \hat\theta_K(r)\ \in\ \operatorname{ArgMax}_K(r), \] where $\hat\theta_K(r)$ denotes an arbitrary (fixed) measurable selection from the nonempty set $\operatorname{ArgMax}_K(r)$.

nodes.name: Restricted maximiser correspondence
nodes.statement: For $u\in[t^\ast,T]$ we also use the restricted correspondence \[ \operatorname{ArgMax}_K^{[u]}(r)\ :=\ \arg\max_{\theta\in K}\ell_r^{[u]}(\theta), \qquad \hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r)\ \in\ \operatorname{ArgMax}_K^{[u]}(r), \] where $\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r)$ denotes an arbitrary (fixed) measurable selection.

nodes.name: Localised restricted M-step selection
nodes.statement: When the feasible set is $K=\Theta_{\rm sc}$ we write $\hat\theta_r^{[u]}:=\hat\theta_{\Theta_{\rm sc}}^{[u]}(r)$.

nodes.name: Localised neighbourhood Theta_sc
nodes.statement: In the local-curvature regime of Assumption~\ref{ass:G6} we will also use the localised neighbourhood \[ \Theta_{\rm sc}:=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc}). \]

nodes.name: Default localised maximiser
nodes.statement: When we write $\hat\theta_r$ without specifying $K$, we mean the localised choice $\hat\theta_r:=\hat\theta_{\Theta_{\rm sc}}(r)$.

nodes.name: Selected-component process
nodes.statement: Define the selected-component process on $[t^\ast,T)$ by \begin{equation} \mathrm{sel}_r(t):=r_{N(t-)+1}\qquad (t\in[t^\ast,T)). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Selected-component process
nodes.statement: \mathrm{sel}_r(t):=r_{N(t-)+1}\qquad (t\in[t^\ast,T)).
nodes.label: eq:sel-def

nodes.name: Hamming distance between labellings
nodes.statement: For two labellings $r,r'\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$, define the (window-restricted) Hamming distance \[ d_H(r,r'):=\sum_{i=1}^{N(D)} \mathbf 1\{r_i\neq r_i'\}. \]

nodes.name: u-restricted Hamming distance
nodes.statement: For $u\in[t^\ast,T]$ we also define the $u$-restricted Hamming distance \[ d_H^{[u]}(r,r'):=\sum_{i:\,t_i\le u} \mathbf 1\{r_i\neq r_i'\}, \qquad\text{so that}\qquad d_H(r,r')=d_H^{[T]}(r,r'). \]

nodes.name: Predictability of the selected component
nodes.statement: Fix a deterministic labelling $r$. Then $t\mapsto \mathrm{sel}_r(t)$ is $\{\mathcal H_{t-}\}$- and $\{\mathcal G_{t-}\}$-predictable on $[t^\ast,T)$ and, at event times $t_i<T$, $\mathrm{sel}_r(t_i-)=r_i$.
nodes.label: lem:sel-predictable

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Since $N$ is adapted, c\`adl\`ag, and simple, $t\mapsto N(t-)$ is predictable and takes integer values with unit jumps. For each $m\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, the set $\{(t,\omega):N(t-,\omega)=m\}$ is predictable, hence the indicator $t\mapsto \mathbbm{1}\{N(t-)=m\}$ is predictable. On $[t^\ast,T)$ we have the pointwise identity with pairwise disjoint predictable supports \[ \mathrm{sel}_r(t)=\sum_{m=0}^\infty r_{m+1} \mathbbm{1}\{N(t-)=m\}. \] Because the supports are disjoint and for each $(\omega,t)$ exactly one indicator equals $1$, this is a countable pointwise sum of predictable indicators; hence it is predictable. Simplicity implies $N(t_i-)=i-1$, whence $\mathrm{sel}_r(t_i-)=r_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Write sel_r as a countable sum of predictable indicators of {N(t-)=m}; simplicity gives sel_r(t_i-)=r_i.

nodes.name: On predictability of sel_r for random iterate labels
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:sel-predictable} treats deterministic labellings $r$. For random iterate labellings $r^{(m)}$, the process $t\mapsto \mathrm{sel}_{r^{(m)}}(t)=r^{(m)}_{N(t-)+1}$ need not be $\mathcal G$-predictable. In what follows, $\mathrm{sel}_r$ is only used inside pathwise algebraic identities, and any resulting selection-remainder term is dominated by stochastic integrals with $\mathcal G$-predictable integrands built from past labels $r_{1:N(t-)}$.
nodes.label: rem:sel-random

nodes.name: Label-induced intensities (formal)
nodes.statement: For $\tau=(t,x)$ and a labelling $r$, define the label-induced intensities using only past labels by \[ \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta):=\lambda_k\!\big(\tau\mid \mathcal H_{t-}\vee\sigma(r_{1:N(t-)});\theta\big),\qquad \widehat\lambda^r:=\widehat\lambda_0^r+\widehat\lambda_1^r. \]

nodes.name: Label-induced counting measures
nodes.statement: For a labelling $r$ and measurable $A\subset \mathcal S$, \[ \widehat N_k^r\big((t_1,t_2]\times A\big) :=\sum_{i: t_1<t_i\le t_2, x_i\in A}\mathbf 1\{r_i=k\},\qquad k\in\{0,1\}. \]

nodes.name: Complete-data log-likelihood
nodes.statement: For a candidate labelling $r$, the complete-data log-likelihood is \begin{equation} \ell_r(\theta) =\sum_{i=1}^{N(D)} \log \widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r\!\big(\gamma_i;\theta\big) -\int_D \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) \mathrm{d}\tau,\qquad f_r(\theta):=|D|^{-1}\ell_r(\theta). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Complete-data log-likelihood
nodes.statement: \ell_r(\theta) =\sum_{i=1}^{N(D)} \log \widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r\!\big(\gamma_i;\theta\big) -\int_D \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) \mathrm{d}\tau,\qquad f_r(\theta):=|D|^{-1}\ell_r(\theta).
nodes.label: eq:cdll

nodes.name: Restricted complete-data log-likelihood
nodes.statement: For $u\in[t^\ast,T]$ define the restricted complete-data log-likelihood and its normalised version by \begin{align} \ell_r^{[u]}(\theta) &:= \sum_{i:\,t_i\le u} \log \widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r\!\big(\gamma_i;\theta\big) -\int_{D^{[u]}} \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) \mathrm{d}\tau, \\ f_r^{[u]}(\theta) &:=|D^{[u]}|^{-1}\,\ell_r^{[u]}(\theta). \nonumber \end{align}

nodes.name: Restricted complete-data log-likelihood
nodes.statement: \ell_r^{[u]}(\theta) &:= \sum_{i:\,t_i\le u} \log \widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r\!\big(\gamma_i;\theta\big) -\int_{D^{[u]}} \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) \mathrm{d}\tau, \\ f_r^{[u]}(\theta) &:=|D^{[u]}|^{-1}\,\ell_r^{[u]}(\theta). \nonumber
nodes.label: eq:cdll-restricted

nodes.name: Oracle and label-induced log-likelihood ratios
nodes.statement: For $\theta\in\Theta$ define the oracle and label-induced log-likelihood ratios \[ s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau):=\log\frac{\lambda_1(\tau\mid \mathcal G_{t-};\theta)}{\lambda_0(\tau\mid \mathcal G_{t-};\theta)},\qquad \tilde s_\theta(\tau;r):=\log\frac{\widehat\lambda_1^r(\tau;\theta)}{\widehat\lambda_0^r(\tau;\theta)}. \]

nodes.name: Decisive sets and ambiguous band
nodes.statement: Given $b>0$, the decisive sets and ambiguous band are \[ S_\theta^+(b)=\{ \tau:\ s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)\ge b \},\quad S_\theta^-(b)=\{ \tau:\ s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)\le -b \},\quad A_\theta(b)=\{ \tau:\ |s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)|\le b \}. \]

nodes.name: Minority label on decisive sets
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta$ and $b>0$. For an event $\gamma_i$: \[ \text{minority}(\gamma_i;\theta,b)= \begin{cases} 0,& \gamma_i\in S_\theta^+(b),\\ 1,& \gamma_i\in S_\theta^-(b),\\ \text{undefined},& \gamma_i\notin S_\theta^+(b)\cup S_\theta^-(b). \end{cases} \]
nodes.label: def:minority

nodes.name: Oracle-aided viewpoint
nodes.statement: The penalty below uses the oracle decisive sets $S_\theta^\pm(b)$; it is therefore not implementable from observed data. We analyse the resulting oracle-aided hard--EM purely to derive sufficient structural conditions for contraction and consistency.
nodes.label: rem:oracle

nodes.name: Parameter net
nodes.statement: For each window $D$, fix a radius $\varepsilon_{\rm net}\le |D|^{-1}$ and an $\varepsilon_{\rm net}$-net $\mathcal N_{\rm net}\subset\Theta_\circ$; let $N_{\rm net}:=|\mathcal N_{\rm net}|$.

nodes.name: Freedman inequality level
nodes.statement: Throughout we write \begin{equation} z_{\rm Fr}:=\log\!\Big(c_0 (1+\eta_{\rm act}) C_{\rm act} |D| \mathfrak{T} (p+2) N_{\rm net}\Big) + \eta_x\log|D|, \end{equation} and for concreteness we take $c_0=10$ and $\eta_x=2$.

nodes.name: Freedman union-bound level z_Fr
nodes.statement: z_{\rm Fr}:=\log\!\Big(c_0 (1+\eta_{\rm act}) C_{\rm act} |D| \mathfrak{T} (p+2) N_{\rm net}\Big) + \eta_x\log|D|,
nodes.label: eq:z-def

nodes.name: Activity and tails
nodes.statement: There exists $C_{\rm act}<\infty$ and $\eta_{\rm act}\in(0,1)$ such that $\mathbb{E} N(D)\le C_{\rm act}|D|$ and \[ \mathbb{P}\!\big(N(D)\ge (1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act} |D|\big)\le e^{-c|D|} \] for some $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $|D|$. Denote \[ E_{\rm act}:=\big\{N(D)\le (1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act} |D|\big\}. \]
nodes.label: ass:G0

nodes.name: Predictable blockwise updates
nodes.statement: Fix a deterministic partition $t^\ast=u_0<u_1<\cdots<u_{\mathfrak{T}}=T$ as in \S\ref{sec:setup}. Along the update path $\{(r^{(m)},\theta^{(m)}): m=0,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\}$ the following hold: \begin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\alph*)] \item \textbf{(Parameter timing)} For each $m\in\{0,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\}$, the update parameter $\theta^{(m)}$ is $\mathcal G_{u_m}$-measurable. \item \textbf{(Progressive, non-revisiting labels)} For each $m\in\{1,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\}$ and each event index $i$ with $t_i\le u_m$, the label $r_i^{(m)}$ is $\mathcal G_{t_i}$-measurable, and labels are never revised: for all $\ell\ge m$, $r_i^{(\ell)}=r_i^{(m)}$ for every $i$ with $t_i\le u_m$. In particular, for each $m$ the vector $(r_1^{(m)},\dots,r_{N^{(m)}}^{(m)})$ is $\mathcal G_{u_m}$-measurable. \end{enumerate} In particular, for every $m$ and every $t\in[t^\ast,u_m)$ the vector of past labels $(r^{(m)}_1,\ldots,r^{(m)}_{N(t-)})$ is $\mathcal G_{t-}$-measurable and hence \[ \mathcal H_{t-}\vee\sigma(r^{(m)}_{1:N(t-)})\ \subseteq\ \mathcal G_{t-}. \] Consequently, for every $m$, every $u\le u_m$, and every $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, the label-induced intensities $\widehat\lambda_k^{r^{(m)}}(\cdot;\theta)$ are $\mathcal G_{t-}$-predictable on $D^{[u]}$.
nodes.label: ass:G0pred

nodes.name: Uniform margins over labellings
nodes.statement: There exist $\underline\mu_\Sigma>0$ and $\underline\mu_k>0$ ($k=0,1$) such that, for a.e.\ $\tau\in D$, all $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, and all deterministic labellings $r$, \[ \widehat\lambda_0^r(\tau;\theta)+\widehat\lambda_1^r(\tau;\theta)\ \ge\ \underline\mu_\Sigma,\qquad \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\ \ge\ \underline\mu_k. \] Write $\underline\mu_{\min}:=\min\{\underline\mu_0,\underline\mu_1\}$.
nodes.label: ass:G1

nodes.name: Oracle positivity
nodes.statement: There exist $\underline\lambda_k>0$ such that $\lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)\ge \underline\lambda_k$ for all $\tau\in D$, $k\in\{0,1\}$, and $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$. Hence $s_\theta^{\rm or}=\log(\lambda_1/\lambda_0)$ is well-defined.
nodes.label: ass:oracle-positivity

nodes.name: Window envelope along the iterate path
nodes.statement: There exist deterministic model constants $L>0$ (temporal memory), $R\ge 0$ (spatial radius; $R=0$ if not applicable), and $C_{\rm base},C_{\rm loc}<\infty$ (depending only on the model class and $\Theta_\circ$). For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the window-count event \[ \Omega_{n}(L,R):=\left\{\ \sup_{\tau=(t,x)\in D}\ N\Big( (t-L,t)\times B_R(x) \Big)\ \le\ n\ \right\}. \] There exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and an exponent $\eta_{\rm win}>0$ such that, with $n_*(|D|):=\lceil c_1\log|D|\rceil$, \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\big(\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)^c\big)\ \le\ c_2 |D|^{-\eta_{\rm win}}. \end{equation} On the event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ we have, simultaneously for all $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, for the oracle intensities $\lambda^\star$ and for all labellings $r\in \mathcal R_{\rm path}^{\rm flip}$, \[ \sup_{\tau\in D}\ \big(\lambda_0^\star+\lambda_1^\star\big)(\tau)\ \le\ K_{\rm win},\qquad \sup_{\tau\in D}\ \big(\widehat\lambda_0^r+\widehat\lambda_1^r\big)(\tau;\theta)\ \le\ K_{\rm win}, \] where \[ K_{\rm win}:=C_{\rm base}+C_{\rm loc} n_*(|D|). \] In particular, on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ we have $K_{\rm win}=O(\log|D|)$.
nodes.label: ass:G2prime

nodes.name: Polynomial window tail
nodes.statement: \mathbb{P}\big(\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)^c\big)\ \le\ c_2 |D|^{-\eta_{\rm win}}.
nodes.label: eqn:etaWin

nodes.name: Remark on the window tail exponent
nodes.statement: In Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime} we only require the existence of $\eta_{\rm win}>0$ such that \cref{eqn:etaWin} holds, thereby providing a polynomially small tail for the window event. This can then be combined with the martingale errors that are controlled via Freedman's inequality. In particular, the exponent $\eta_x>1$ that appears in the definition of the Freedman inequality level $z_{\rm Fr}$ is not constrained by $\eta_{\rm win}$.

nodes.name: Single-flip locality and influence
nodes.statement:
For any single flip at an event location $\zeta$, with $\Delta\widehat\lambda^r=\widehat\lambda^{r'}-\widehat\lambda^{r}$ and $\Delta\widehat\lambda_{k}^r=\widehat\lambda_{k}^{r'}-\widehat\lambda_{k}^{r}$, there exist finite constants \[ B_\infty,\ B_1,\ B_2,\qquad B_\infty^{m comp},\ B_1^{m comp},\ B_2^{m comp},\qquad B_1^\Sigma,\ B_2^\Sigma \] such that \[ \|\Delta\widehat\lambda^r\|_\infty\le B_\infty,\quad \int_D |\Delta\widehat\lambda^r| \mathrm{d}	au\le B_1,\quad \int_D  rac{(\Delta\widehat\lambda^r)^2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} \mathrm{d}	au\le B_2, \] and, for $k\in\{0,1\}$, \[ \|\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r\|_\infty\le B_\infty^{m comp},\quad \int_D |\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r| \mathrm{d}	au\le B_1^{m comp},\quad \int_D  rac{(\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r)^2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} \mathrm{d}	au\le B_2^{m comp}, \] as well as $\sum_k \int_D |\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r| \mathrm{d}	au \le B_1^\Sigma$ and $\sum_k \int_D  rac{(\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r)^2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} \mathrm{d}	au \le B_2^\Sigma$. In addition (and used when $
abla\log\widehat\lambda_k$ denominators appear), there exist finite constants $\widetilde B_2^{m comp}<\infty$ and $\widetilde B_2^\Sigma<\infty$ such that, for each $k$, \[ \int_D  rac{(\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r)^2}{\underline\mu_k}\,\mathrm{d}	au \ \le\ \widetilde B_2^{m comp}, \qquad \sum_{k=0}^1 \int_D  rac{(\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r)^2}{\underline\mu_k}\,\mathrm{d}	au \ \le\ \widetilde B_2^\Sigma. \] In terms of the gradient-level analogues, there exist finite constants \[ \overline B_\infty^{m comp},\ \overline B_1^{m comp},\ \overline B_2^{m comp},\qquad \overline B_1^\Sigma \] such that, for each component $k$, \[ \|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r)\|_\infty\le \overline B_\infty^{m comp},\quad \int_D \|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r)\| \mathrm{d}	au\le \overline B_1^{m comp},\quad \int_D  rac{\|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r)\|^2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma} \mathrm{d}	au\le \overline B_2^{m comp}, \] and $\sum_k\int_D \|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r)\| \mathrm{d}	au\le \overline B_1^\Sigma$. Define the total-gradient difference $\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda^{r}):=\sum_{k=0}^1 \Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^{r})$. Then, for notational convenience, introduce finite constants $\overline B_\infty^\Sigma$ and $\overline B_2^\Sigma$ such that \[ \|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda^{r})\|_\infty\le \overline B_\infty^\Sigma, \qquad \int_D  rac{\|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda^{r})\|^2}{\underline\mu_\Sigma}\,\mathrm{d}	au\le \overline B_2^\Sigma. \] For instance, one may take $\overline B_\infty^\Sigma:=2\overline B_\infty^{m comp}$ and $\overline B_2^\Sigma:=4\overline B_2^{m comp}$. Furthermore, there exists $S_\infty<\infty$ and $H_\infty < \infty$ such that \[ \operatorname*{ess sup}_{	au,k,	heta,r}\ \|
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r(	au;	heta)\|\ \le\ S_\infty, \qquad \operatorname*{ess sup}_{	au,k,	heta,r}\ \|
abla^2_{	heta	heta} \widehat\lambda_k^r(	au;	heta)\|\ \le\ H_\infty. \] The same bounds hold when $\widehat\lambda_k^r(	au;	heta)$ is replaced by the oracle intensity $\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta)$. Finally, there exist finite constants $\widetilde{\overline B}_2^{m comp}<\infty$ such that, for each $k$, \[ \int_D  rac{\|\Delta(
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda_k^r)\|^2}{\underline\mu_k}\,\mathrm{d}	au \ \le\ \widetilde{\overline B}_2^{m comp}. \]
nodes.label: ass:G3

nodes.name: Uniform score alignment
nodes.statement: There exist a deterministic sequence \(\Delta_s(|D|)\ge 0\), an exponent \(\eta>0\), and events \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\) with \(\mathbb P(E^{\rm align}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}\) such that, on \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\), uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_\circ\), all deterministic labellings \(r\), and a.e.\ \(\tau\in D\), \[ \big|\tilde s_\theta(\tau;r)-s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)\big|\ \le\ \Delta_s(|D|). \] For brevity, on \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\) we write \(\Delta_s:=\Delta_s(|D|)\).
nodes.label: ass:G4

nodes.name: Consequence on decisive sets
nodes.statement: On the event \(E^{\rm align}_{|D|}\), Assumption~\ref{ass:G4} implies that, for any \(b>0\), \[ \tau\in S_\theta^+(b)\Rightarrow \tilde s_\theta(\tau;r)\ge b-\Delta_s, \qquad \tau\in S_\theta^-(b)\Rightarrow \tilde s_\theta(\tau;r)\le -b+\Delta_s. \] In particular, if \(b\ge \Delta_s\) then \(\tilde s_\theta(\cdot;r)\) and \(s_\theta^{\rm or}(\cdot)\) have the same sign on \(S_\theta^+(b)\cup S_\theta^-(b)\).

nodes.name: LLR Lipschitz in theta (average-case)
nodes.statement: There exist a deterministic sequence $L_s(|D|)<\infty$, an $\eta>0$, and events $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$ with $\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}$ such that, for all $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{\rm sc}$, \[ \int_D |s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}(\tau)|\,\lambda^\star(\tau)\,d\tau \le L_s(|D|)\,|D|\,\|\theta-\theta'\|. \] Moreover, on the same event $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$ the bound holds uniformly on the deterministic schedule subwindows: for every $m\in\{1,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\}$ and all $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{\rm sc}$, \begin{align*} \int_{D^{(m)}} \big| s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}(\tau) \big| \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau \ \le&\ L_s(|D|)\, |D^{(m)}| \|\theta-\theta'\|,\\ \int_{D_m} \big| s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}(\tau) \big| \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau \ \le&\ L_s(|D|)\, |D_m| \|\theta-\theta'\|. \end{align*}
nodes.label: ass:G5

nodes.name: LLR Lipschitz constant shorthand
nodes.statement: On the event $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$ in Assumption~\ref{ass:G5}, we write $L_s:=L_s(|D|)$ for brevity.

nodes.name: Local strong concavity and near-zero score at r*
nodes.statement:
There exist constants $r_{m sc}>0$, $m_{m sc}>0$, $C_{m sc}<\infty$, and $\eta>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $|D|$, there is an event $E^{m sc}_{|D|}$ with $\mathbb{P}(E^{m sc}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}$ on which:  egin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\alph*)] \item 	extbf{(Uniform local curvature)} $f_{r^\star}$ is differentiable on \[ \Theta_{m sc}:=\Theta_\circ\cap B(	heta^\star,r_{m sc}), \qquad B(	heta^\star,r_{m sc}):=\{	heta\in\mathbb{R}^p:\ \|	heta-	heta^\star\|\le r_{m sc}\}, \] and satisfies the gradient monotonicity inequality  egin{equation}  ig(
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta')-
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta) ig)^	op(	heta'-	heta) \ \le\ -m_{m sc}\|	heta'-	heta\|^2 \qquad orall	heta,	heta'\in\Theta_{m sc}. \end{equation} If $f_{r^\star}$ is twice differentiable, a sufficient condition for \eqref{eq:RSC-grad} is the uniform Hessian bound $-
abla^2 f_{r^\star}(	heta)\succeq m_{m sc}I_p$ for all $	heta\in\Theta_{m sc}$. \item 	extbf{(Score at the truth)} \[ \|
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta^\star)\|\ \le\ C_{m sc}\!\left(\sqrt{ rac{K_{m win} z_{m Fr}}{|D|}} +  rac{z_{m Fr}}{|D|}ight)\!, \] where $K_{m win}$ is as in \cref{ass:G2prime}. In bounded-intensity settings, the score bound in (b) follows from Lemma~ef{lem:score-nearzero} on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ by choosing $z_{m Fr}\simeq \log|D|$ (and using $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)^c)\le c_2|D|^{-\eta_{m win}}$ from Assumption~ef{ass:G2prime}). \item 	extbf{(Uniformity over deterministic prefixes)} For every $m\in\{1,\dots,\mathfrak{T}\}$, the conclusions in (a) and (b) also hold with the full-window objective $f_{r^\star}$ replaced by the prefix objective $f_{r^\star}^{[u_m]}$, with the same constants $r_{m sc},m_{m sc},C_{m sc}$, and with $|D|$ replaced by $|D^{(m)}|=|D^{[u_m]}|$ in the score bound. \end{enumerate} Further, assume $	heta^\star$ lies in a compact subset of $\Theta_\circ$ bounded away from any non-identifiability/collision boundary. Equivalently, there exists $\delta_{m sep}>0$ such that $\mathrm{dist}(	heta^\star,\partial\Theta_{m id})\ge \delta_{m sep}$, and choose $r_{m sc}\le \delta_{m sep}/2$.
nodes.label: ass:G6

nodes.name: Gradient monotonicity inequality
nodes.statement: \big(\nabla f_{r^\star}(\theta')-\nabla f_{r^\star}(\theta)\big)^\top(\theta'-\theta) \ \le\ -m_{\rm sc}\|\theta'-\theta\|^2 \qquad\forall\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{\rm sc}.
nodes.label: eq:RSC-grad

nodes.name: On concavity restrictions
nodes.statement: In Hawkes models, global log-likelihood concavity typically holds for parameters that enter linearly (e.g.\ baselines and excitation amplitudes) but can fail for nonlinear parameters such as the decay rate $\beta$. Accordingly, rather than imposing global concavity on $\Theta_\circ$, we use the local condition in Assumption~\ref{ass:G6}: it suffices that $f_{r^\star}$ is uniformly strongly concave on a deterministic-radius neighborhood $\Theta_{\rm sc}=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc})$, and we then keep all iterates inside $\Theta_{\rm sc}$ via an invariant-set argument.
nodes.label: rem:concavity-beta

nodes.name: Warm start
nodes.statement: The initialization satisfies $\|\theta^{(0)}-\theta^\star\|\le r_{\rm sc}$ (equivalently $\theta^{(0)}\in\Theta_{\rm sc}$).
nodes.label: ass:warmstart

nodes.name: Why the warm start is reasonable
nodes.statement: This warm-start condition motivates the requirement that the process/history up to \(t^\star\) is observed: if one can construct a pilot estimator \(\tilde\theta_0\) from the data on \([0,t^\star]\times\mathcal S\) such that $\tilde\theta_0$ is consistent for the initial parameter $\theta_0^\star$ (and in our setting $\theta_0^\star=\theta^\star$), then for sufficiently large sample size (or amount of data) we have $\|\tilde\theta_0-\theta^\star\|\le r_{\rm sc}$ with high probability. Thus, taking $\theta^{(0)}:=\tilde\theta_0$ makes Assumption~\ref{ass:warmstart} operational.
nodes.label: rem:warmstart

nodes.name: Canonical telescoping path
nodes.statement: Given two labellings $r,r^\star\in\{0,1\}^{N(D)}$, let $I:=\{ i\in\{1,\dots,N(D)\}:\ r_i\neq r_i^\star \}$ and $\mathfrak{I}:=|I|$. Fix a deterministic ordering of $I$ (e.g., increasing index), write $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_\mathfrak{I})$, and define a sequence $(r^{(j)})_{j=0}^{\mathfrak I}$ by $r^{(0)}:=r$, \[r^{(j)}:=\text{ the labelling obtained from } r^{(j-1)} \text{ by flipping only coordinate } i_j \quad (j=1,\ldots,\mathfrak{I}). \] We call $(r^{(0)},r^{(1)},\ldots,r^{(\mathfrak{I})})$ the canonical telescoping path from $r$ to $r^\star$. It has length $\mathfrak{I}=d_H(r,r^\star)$ and ends at $r^{(\mathfrak{I})}=r^\star$. For any functional $F$ on labellings, \[ F(r)-F(r^\star)=\sum_{j=1}^\mathfrak{I} \big(F(r^{(j-1)})-F(r^{(j)})\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Flip the disagreeing coordinates of r one at a time in a fixed order to reach r*; any functional difference telescopes along it.
nodes.label: def:telescoping-path

nodes.name: Label-to-score Lipschitz
nodes.label: ass:G7prime

nodes.name: Decisive-set disagreement set
nodes.statement: For $b>0$ and any $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, define \[ B_\theta\ :=\ \big(S_{\theta^\star}^+(b) \Delta S_{\theta}^+(b)\big)\ \cup\ \big(S_{\theta^\star}^-(b) \Delta S_{\theta}^-(b)\big). \]
nodes.label: def:Btheta

nodes.name: Mass on decisive sets and oracle-set concentration
nodes.statement: All expectations and probabilities in this assumption are with respect to $P_{\theta^\star}$. There exist \(\eta>0\), \(c>0\), \(C_{\rm it}>0\), and, for each threshold \(b=b_{|D|}>0\) used in the theorem under consideration, nonnegative sequences \[ \eta_+(|D|;b),\qquad \eta_-(|D|;b), \] such that \(\mathfrak{T}=\lceil C_{\rm it}\log|D|\rceil\), and the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\roman*)] \item \textbf{(Minority mass on oracle decisive sets at threshold \(b\)).} \[ \mathbb{E} N_0\!\big(S_{\theta^\star}^+(b)\big)\ \le\ \eta_+(|D|;b)\,|D|, \qquad \mathbb{E} N_1\!\big(S_{\theta^\star}^-(b)\big)\ \le\ \eta_-(|D|;b)\,|D|. \] Since $S_{\theta^\star}^\pm(b)\subseteq S_{\theta^\star}^\pm(b_{\rm th})$ for $b\ge b_{\rm th}$, the bounds for $b_{\rm th}$ imply the same bounds for $b$. \item \textbf{(Concentration for fixed oracle sets and iterate-dependent disagreement sets).} Moreover, for all $\delta\in(0,1)$ and for $S$ ranging over the oracle sets \[ \mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b):=\big\{S_{\theta^\star}^+(b), S_{\theta^\star}^-(b), A_{\theta^\star}(b), A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\big\}, \] we have oracle-set concentration simultaneously for total and component counts around their means: \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|N(S)-\mathbb{E} N(S)\right|\ge \delta|D|\right)\le& \exp\left(-c \frac{\delta^2|D|}{K_{\rm win}}\right),\\ \mathbb{P}\!\left(\left|N_k(S)-\mathbb{E} N_k(S)\right|\ge \delta|D|\right)\le& \exp\left(-c \frac{\delta^2|D|}{K_{\rm win}}\right) \end{align*} for $k\in\{0,1\}$. Define the mean-deviation event \begin{align*} E^{\rm mean}_{|D|} &:= \bigcap_{S\in\mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b)} \left\{ \left|N(S)-\mathbb{E} N(S)\right|\le C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|D|\log|D|} \right\} \\ &\quad\cap \bigcap_{k=0}^1\bigcap_{S\in\mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b)} \left\{ \left|N_k(S)-\mathbb{E} N_k(S)\right|\le C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|D|\log|D|} \right\}. \end{align*} Assume $\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm mean}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}$ for some $\eta>0$ (finite union over $\mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b)$). We also require concentration around compensators for the same fixed oracle sets and for the iterate-dependent disagreement sets. Define $E^{\rm comp}_{|D|}$ to be the event on which the following hold simultaneously: \begin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\alph*)] \item for all $S\in\mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b)$ and all $k\in\{0,1\}$, \begin{align*} \Big|N_k(S)-\int_S \lambda_k^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\Big| \le& C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|D|\log|D|},\\ \Big|N(S)-\int_S\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\Big| \le& C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|D|\log|D|}; \end{align*} \item for all iterates $m\in\{0,\dots,\mathfrak{T}-1\}$, \[ \Big|N(B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1}) -\int_{B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1}}\lambda^\star(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau\Big| \le C_{\rm it}\sqrt{K_{\rm win}|D_{m+1}|\log|D|}. \] \end{enumerate} Assume $\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm comp}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}$ for some (possibly different) $\eta>0$. Finally set \[ E^{\rm mass}_{|D|}\ :=\ E^{\rm mean}_{|D|}\cap E^{\rm comp}_{|D|}, \] and assume $\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm mass}_{|D|})\ge 1-|D|^{-\eta}$ for some $\eta>0$. \end{enumerate} All expectation and concentration statements above are also assumed to hold uniformly when the observation window is replaced by any deterministic prefix window $D^{(m)}$ or deterministic block $D_m$ from the schedule. Equivalently, we may replace any set $S\subset D$ appearing above by $S\cap W$ and replace $|D|$ by $|W|$ for any $W\in\{D^{(m)},D_m\}$, with the same constants (and with the corresponding $N(W)$-type counts). In particular, we include in $E^{\rm comp}_{|D|}$ the compensator deviations for the restricted fixed oracle sets $S\cap D_m$ (for $S\in\mathcal F_{\rm fixed}(b)$) and, for iterate-dependent disagreement sets, the blockwise deviations on $B_{\theta^{(m)}}\cap D_{m+1}$ as in (b). Since the schedule is deterministic and has size $O(\mathfrak{T})$, these additional requirements are absorbed by a finite union.
nodes.label: ass:G8

nodes.name: Existence of M-step maximisers
nodes.statement: Work on the window-envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ from Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime}. Let $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$ be any labelling on the iterate path and let $u\in[t^\ast,T]$. \begin{enumerate}[nosep,label=(\alph*)] \item The map $\theta\mapsto \ell_r^{[u]}(\theta)$ is continuous on $\Theta_\circ$ and hence attains a maximum on $\Theta_\circ$. Consequently $\operatorname{ArgMax}_{\Theta_\circ}^{[u]}(r)$ is nonempty. \item Let $\Theta_{\rm sc}:=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc})$ as in Assumption~\ref{ass:G6} and suppose $\Theta_{\rm sc}\neq\emptyset$. Then $\theta\mapsto \ell_r^{[u]}(\theta)$ also attains a maximum on $\Theta_{\rm sc}$, so $\operatorname{ArgMax}_{\Theta_{\rm sc}}^{[u]}(r)$ is nonempty. \item Taking $u=T$ yields the same conclusions for the full-window objective $\ell_r=\ell_r^{[T]}$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Work on the window-envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ from Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime}.
Let $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$ be any labelling on the iterate path and let $u\in[t^\ast,T]$.
conclusions: The map $\theta\mapsto \ell_r^{[u]}(\theta)$ is continuous on $\Theta_\circ$ and hence attains a maximum on $\Theta_\circ$.
nodes.label: lem:existence-M

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Fix $u\in[t^\ast,T]$ and $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$. By Assumption~\ref{ass:G1}, $\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r(\gamma_i;\theta)\ge \underline\mu_{\min}$ for all $i$ and $\theta$, so $\theta\mapsto \log\widehat\lambda_{r_i}^r(\gamma_i;\theta)$ is continuous. On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime} provides a deterministic bound $K_{\rm win}$ such that $\sum_{k=0}^1\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\le K_{\rm win}$ for all $\tau\in D$, all $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$, and all $r\in\mathcal R_{\rm path}$. Since $\theta\mapsto \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)$ is continuous for each $\tau$, dominated convergence (dominated by $K_{\rm win}$ on the finite-measure set $D^{[u]}$) implies continuity of \[ \theta\ \longmapsto\ \int_{D^{[u]}} \sum_{k=0}^1 \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\,\mathrm{d}\tau . \] Therefore $\ell_r^{[u]}$ is continuous on $\Theta_\circ$. Since $\Theta_\circ$ is compact, $\ell_r^{[u]}$ attains a maximum on $\Theta_\circ$. The same argument applies on the compact set $\Theta_{\rm sc}=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc})$. Finally, taking $u=T$ recovers $\ell_r=\ell_r^{[T]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Margins give continuity of the log terms, the window envelope gives dominated convergence for the compensator; compactness yields maximisers.

nodes.name: M-step optimality condition and differentiability
nodes.statement: For every labelling $r$ on the iterate path $\mathcal R_{\rm path}$ and every $u\in[t^\ast,T]$, the objective $f_r^{[u]}$ admits a $C^1$ extension to an open neighbourhood of $\Theta_\circ$. For any convex constraint set $K\in\{\Theta_\circ,\Theta_{\rm sc}\}$ and any maximiser $\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r)\in\arg\max_{\theta\in K}\ell_r^{[u]}(\theta)$, the (global) first-order optimality condition holds: \[ (\theta-\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r))^\top \nabla f_r^{[u]}(\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r))\ \le\ 0 \qquad\text{for all }\theta\in K. \] In particular, if $\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r)\in\operatorname{int}(K)$ then $\nabla f_r^{[u]}(\hat\theta_K^{[u]}(r))=0$. Taking $u=T$ recovers the same condition for the full-window objective $f_r$.
nodes.label: ass:G9

nodes.name: Why the variational inequality is automatic
nodes.statement: The feasible set $\Theta_{\rm sc}:=\Theta_\circ\cap B(\theta^\star,r_{\rm sc})$ is convex since $\Theta_\circ$ is convex. Negative definiteness of the Hessian (equivalently, local strong concavity) is only required on \(\Theta_{\rm sc}\) (Assumption~\ref{ass:G6}); possible degeneracies elsewhere in \(\Theta_\circ\) are irrelevant provided the iterates remain in $\Theta_{\rm sc}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:inv-sc}). For any convex constraint set $K$ and any maximiser $\hat\theta_K(r)\in\arg\max_{\theta\in K}\ell_r(\theta)$, the standard first-order necessary condition for constrained maximisation gives \[ (\theta-\hat\theta_K(r))^\top \nabla f_r(\hat\theta_K(r))\le 0\qquad\text{for all }\theta\in K. \] In particular, if $\hat\theta_K(r)\in \operatorname{int}(K)$ then $\nabla f_r(\hat\theta_K(r))=0$.

nodes.name: Optional margin assumption for the band
nodes.statement: In some applications, one can assume the oracle margin: there exist $\alpha_{\rm band}>0$ and $C_{\rm band}<\infty$ such that for all small $u>0$, \[ \frac{1}{|D|}\int_D \mathbbm{1}\{|s_{\theta^\star}^{\rm or}(\tau)|\le u\} \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau\ \le\ C_{\rm band} u^{\alpha_{\rm band}}. \] Under this assumption and the oracle-set concentration in \cref{ass:G8}, with high probability \[N(A_{\theta^\star}(2b))/|D|\lesssim C_{\rm band} (2b)^{\alpha_{\rm band}} + O\left(\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win}\log|D|}{|D|}}\right)\] for those $b$ with $2b$ in the validity range of the margin bound.
nodes.label: rem:margin

nodes.name: Ambiguous-band mass
nodes.statement: For any $b>0$ define \[ C_b(\theta^\star)\ :=\ \frac{1}{|D|}\int_D \mathbbm{1}\{|s_{\theta^\star}^{\rm or}(\tau)|\le 2b\} \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau. \] By \cref{ass:G8}, we have $|D|^{-1}N\!\big(A_{\theta^\star}(2b)\big)=C_b(\theta^\star)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)$ as $|D|\to\infty$.
nodes.label: def:C_b

nodes.name: Indicator of a post-stopping-time interval is predictable
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma$ be a stopping time (with respect to the filtration in force). Then the set $\{(t,\omega):t>\sigma(\omega)\}$ is predictable. Equivalently, $t\mapsto \mathbbm{1}\{t>\sigma\}$ is predictable.
assumptions: Let $\sigma$ be a stopping time (with respect to the filtration in force).
nodes.label: lem:predictable-stoptime

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Define $X_t:=\mathbbm{1}\{t>\sigma\}$. Since $\sigma$ is a stopping time, $\{\sigma\le q\}\in\mathcal F_q$ for all $q$. Moreover, for each $t$, \[ \{X_t=1\}=\{\sigma<t\}=\bigcup_{\substack{q\in\mathbb Q\\ q<t}}\{\sigma\le q\}\in\mathcal F_t, \] so $(X_t)$ is adapted. Moreover $X$ is left-continuous: $X_\sigma=0$ and for $t\uparrow\sigma$ we have $X_t=0$. Every adapted left-continuous process is predictable, hence $X$ is predictable.
nodes.statement_short: The indicator is adapted (via rational approximation of {sigma<t}) and left-continuous, hence predictable.

nodes.name: Freedman inequality for point-process martingales
nodes.statement: Let $M^\star$ be the compensated martingale of $N$ and let $h$ be $\mathcal G$-predictable with $\|h\|_\infty\le H<\infty$. Set \[ X_T=\int_D h\,\mathrm{d} M^\star,\qquad V=\int_D h^2 \lambda^\star\,\mathrm{d}\tau. \] Then, for any $z_{\rm Fr}>0$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\!\left(X_T \ge \frac{H}{3} z_{\rm Fr} + \sqrt{ 2Vz_{\rm Fr} + \frac{H^2}{9}z_{\rm Fr}^2 }\right)\le& e^{-z_{\rm Fr}},\\ \mathbb{P}\!\left(|X_T| \ge \frac{H}{3} z_{\rm Fr} + \sqrt{ 2Vz_{\rm Fr} + \frac{H^2}{9}z_{\rm Fr}^2 }\right)\le& 2e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}. \end{align*} The same bounds hold when $M^\star$ is replaced by either component martingale $M_k^\star$ and $\lambda^\star$ by $\lambda_k^\star$.
assumptions: Let $M^\star$ be the compensated martingale of $N$ and let $h$ be $\mathcal G$-predictable with $\|h\|_\infty\le H<\infty$.
conclusions: The same bounds hold when $M^\star$ is replaced by either component martingale $M_k^\star$ and $\lambda^\star$ by $\lambda_k^\star$.
nodes.statement_short: Bernstein-Freedman tail bound for stochastic integrals of bounded predictable integrands against the compensated point-process martingale.
nodes.label: lem:Freedman

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: This is a standard continuous time analogue of Freedman inequality for martingales with bounded jumps and predictable quadratic characteristic \citep{freedman1975tail}, the properties of which are discussed in depth in \citet{DZHAPARIDZE2001109}.
nodes.statement_short: Cites the continuous-time Freedman inequality.

nodes.name: Near-zero oracle score at the truth via Freedman
nodes.statement: Assume oracle positivity (Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle-positivity}) and the oracle gradient bound in Assumption~\ref{ass:G3}. Fix $z_{\rm Fr}>0$ and work on the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ of Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime}, so that $\sup_{\tau\in D}\lambda^\star(\tau)\le K_{\rm win}$. Then with probability at least $1-4p\,e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}$ (conditional on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$), \[ \|\nabla f_{r^\star}(\theta^\star)\| \ \le\ C_{\rm sc}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}} + \frac{z_{\rm Fr}}{|D|}\right), \] where one may take \[ C_{\rm sc}\ :=\ \frac{8\sqrt{2p}\,S_\infty}{\underline\lambda_{\min}}, \qquad \underline\lambda_{\min}:=\min\{\underline\lambda_0,\underline\lambda_1\}. \]
assumptions: Assume oracle positivity (Assumption~\ref{ass:oracle-positivity}) and the oracle gradient bound in Assumption~\ref{ass:G3}.
work on the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ of Assumption~\ref{ass:G2prime}
conclusions: Then with probability at least $1-4p\,e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}$ (conditional on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$),
nodes.statement_short: The normalised oracle score at the truth is O(sqrt(K_win z_Fr/|D|) + z_Fr/|D|) with high probability.
nodes.label: lem:score-nearzero

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement:
Write $\lambda_k^\star(	au):=\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta^\star)$ and recall that under $r^\star$ (the true labels) the complete-data log-likelihood is \[ \ell_{r^\star}(	heta)=\sum_{k=0}^1\left(\int_D \log\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta)\,dN_k(	au) -\int_D \lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta)\,d	auight). \] Differentiating and evaluating at $	heta^\star$ gives \[ 
abla \ell_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) =\sum_{k=0}^1\left(\int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta^\star)\,dN_k(	au) -\int_D 
abla_	heta\lambda_k(	au\mid\mathcal G_{t-};	heta^\star)\,d	auight). \] Using the Doob--Meyer decomposition $dN_k=dM_k^\star+\lambda_k^\star\,d	au$ and the identity $
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k=(
abla_	heta\lambda_k)/\lambda_k$, we obtain the cancellation \[ \int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k^\star\,\lambda_k^\star\,d	au =\int_D 
abla_	heta\lambda_k^\star\,d	au, \] hence  egin{equation} 
abla \ell_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) =\sum_{k=0}^1\int_D 
abla_	heta\log\lambda_k^\star(	au)\,dM_k^\star(	au). \end{equation} Dividing by $|D|$ yields the same representation for $
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta^\star)$. Fix a coordinate $j\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ and define the predictable integrand \[ h_{k,j}(	au):=\partial_{	heta_j}\log\lambda_k^\star(	au) = rac{\partial_{	heta_j}\lambda_k^\star(	au)}{\lambda_k^\star(	au)}. \] By oracle positivity, $\lambda_k^\star(	au)\ge \underline\lambda_k\ge \underline\lambda_{\min}$, and by the oracle gradient bound in Assumption~ef{ass:G3}, $\|
abla_	heta\lambda_k^\star(	au)\|\le S_\infty$ a.e.; therefore \[ |h_{k,j}(	au)| \le  rac{\|
abla_	heta\lambda_k^\star(	au)\|}{\lambda_k^\star(	au)} \le  rac{S_\infty}{\underline\lambda_{\min}} =:H. \] On the window envelope event $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ we have $\lambda_k^\star(	au)\le \lambda^\star(	au)\le K_{m win}$, so the predictable quadratic characteristic of $\int_D h_{k,j}\,dM_k^\star$ satisfies \[ V_{k,j} :=\int_D h_{k,j}(	au)^2\,\lambda_k^\star(	au)\,d	au \le \int_D H^2\,\lambda_k^\star(	au)\,d	au \le H^2\,K_{m win}\,|D|. \] Apply Lemma~ef{lem:Freedman} (two-sided form) to the scalar martingale integral $X_{k,j}:=\int_D h_{k,j}\,dM_k^\star$. On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, with probability at least $1-2e^{-z_{m Fr}}$, \[ |X_{k,j}| \le  rac{H}{3}z_{m Fr}+\sqrt{2V_{k,j}z_{m Fr}+ rac{H^2}{9}z_{m Fr}^2} \le  rac{H}{3}z_{m Fr}+\sqrt{2H^2K_{m win}|D|\,z_{m Fr}+ rac{H^2}{9}z_{m Fr}^2}. \] Using $\sqrt{a+b}\le \sqrt a+\sqrt b$ and $\sqrt{H^2}=H$ gives \[ |X_{k,j}| \le H\sqrt{2K_{m win}|D|\,z_{m Fr}}+ rac{2H}{3}z_{m Fr}. \] Now union bound over the $2p$ pairs $(k,j)$ yields that, on $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$, with probability at least $1-4p\,e^{-z_{m Fr}}$ the above bound holds simultaneously for all $k\in\{0,1\}$ and $j\in\{1,\dots,p\}$. On this event, for each coordinate $j$ we combine \eqref{eq:score-mtg-rep} with the triangle inequality: \[  ig|\partial_{	heta_j}\ell_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) ig| =\left|\sum_{k=0}^1 X_{k,j}ight| \le \sum_{k=0}^1|X_{k,j}| \le 2H\sqrt{2K_{m win}|D|\,z_{m Fr}}+ rac{4H}{3}z_{m Fr}. \] Dividing by $|D|$ yields \[  ig|\partial_{	heta_j} f_{r^\star}(	heta^\star) ig| \le 2H\sqrt{ rac{2K_{m win}z_{m Fr}}{|D|}}+ rac{4H}{3} rac{z_{m Fr}}{|D|}. \] Finally, $\|
abla f\|\le \sqrt p\,\max_j|\partial_{	heta_j} f|$, hence \[ \|
abla f_{r^\star}(	heta^\star)\| \le \sqrt p\left(2H\sqrt{ rac{2K_{m win}z_{m Fr}}{|D|}}+ rac{4H}{3} rac{z_{m Fr}}{|D|}ight) \le  rac{8\sqrt{2p}\,S_\infty}{\underline\lambda_{\min}} \left(\sqrt{ rac{K_{m win}z_{m Fr}}{|D|}}+ rac{z_{m Fr}}{|D|}ight), \] which is the claimed bound with the stated choice of $C_{m sc}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write the score at theta* as a martingale integral via Doob-Meyer, bound each coordinate by Freedman, union bound over coordinates.

nodes.name: Martingale representation of the oracle score
nodes.statement: \nabla \ell_{r^\star}(\theta^\star) =\sum_{k=0}^1\int_D \nabla_\theta\log\lambda_k^\star(\tau)\,dM_k^\star(\tau).
nodes.label: eq:score-mtg-rep

nodes.name: Stochastic Fubini for v-interpolation
nodes.statement: Let $H(\tau,v)$ be jointly measurable in $(\tau,v)\in D\times[0,1]$, $\mathcal G$-predictable in $\tau$ for each $v$, and $\sup_{v\in[0,1]}\|H(\cdot,v)\|_\infty<\infty$. Suppose moreover that \[ \int_0^1\!\!\int_D H(\tau,v)^2 \lambda^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d}\tau \mathrm{d} v\ <\ \infty. \] Then \[ \int_0^1\!\!\int_D H(\tau,v) \mathrm{d} M^\star(\tau) \mathrm{d} v\ =\ \int_D\!\Big(\int_0^1 H(\tau,v) \mathrm{d} v\Big) \mathrm{d} M^\star(\tau) \] almost surely, and the right-hand side is square-integrable \citep{protter2012stochastic}.
assumptions: Let $H(\tau,v)$ be jointly measurable in $(\tau,v)\in D\times[0,1]$, $\mathcal G$-predictable in $\tau$ for each $v$, and $\sup_{v\in[0,1]}\|H(\cdot,v)\|_\infty<\infty$.
conclusions: almost surely, and the right-hand side is square-integrable \citep{protter2012stochastic}.
nodes.label: lem:stoch-fubini

nodes.name: Deterministic Lipschitz bounds in theta for common integrands
nodes.statement: Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:G1} and~\ref{ass:G3}.
