A union bound over the finite grid $\mathcal G$ yields \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}\Bigl( \max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G} N(W_{s,y})>n \Bigr) \;\le\; |\mathcal G|\,M e^{-\theta n} \;\le\; C_{\rm grid} M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over enlarged grid windows (eq. 40)
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Cover arbitrary windows
nodes.statement: For any $(t,x)\in D$, choose $s\in\mathsf{T}$ and $y\in\mathcal X$ such that \[ |t-s|\le \Delta_t = h/2,\qquad \|x-y\|\le R/2. \] Then $B_R(x)\subset B_{3R/2}(y)\subset B_{2R}(y)$ and \[ [t-h,t] \subset [s-2h,s+h]. \] The interval $[s-2h,s+h]$ is contained in the union of three intervals of length $h$, for example $[s-2h,s-h]$, $[s-h,s]$, and $[s,s+h]$. Hence \[ [t-h,t]\times B_R(x) \subset \bigcup_{\ell=1}^3 \bigl([s_\ell-h,s_\ell]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr), \] for suitable $s_\ell\in\mathsf{T}'$ in a time grid $\mathsf{T}'$ obtained by shifting $\mathsf{T}$ by multiples of $h$. Enlarging $\mathcal G$ if necessary to \( \mathcal G':=\mathsf{T}'\times\mathcal X, \) we obtain \[ N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) \;\le\; 3\max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr). \] The cardinality of $\mathcal G'$ is still bounded by a constant multiple of $|D|$: $|\mathcal G'|\le C'_{\rm grid}|D|$ for some $C'_{\rm grid}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Any window is covered by three grid windows
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Supremum bound
nodes.statement: Taking a supremum over $(t,x)\in D$ yields \[ \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) \;\le\; 3\max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr). \] Therefore, \[ \mathbb{P}\!\left( \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) > 3n \right) \;\le\; \mathbb{P}\!\left( \max_{(s,y)\in\mathcal G'} N\bigl([s-h,s]\times B_{2R}(y)\bigr) > n \right). \] Applying \eqref{eq:grid-union-app} (with $\mathcal G'$ and possibly a different grid constant) gives \[ \mathbb{P}\!\left( \sup_{(t,x)\in D} N\bigl([t-h,t]\times B_R(x)\bigr) > 3n \right) \;\le\; C''_{\rm grid} M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n} \] for some $C''_{\rm grid}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the supremum and apply the grid union bound
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Choose n_*
nodes.statement: Finally, let $\eta>0$ be arbitrary and choose \[ n = n_0(|D|) := \Bigl\lceil \frac{\eta+1}{\theta}\,\log|D| \Bigr\rceil. \] Then \[ C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|\,e^{-\theta n} \;\le\; C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|\,e^{-(\eta+1)\log|D|} \;=\; C''_{\rm grid}M\,|D|^{-\eta}. \] Absorbing the multiplicative constant $3$ in front of $n$ into the definition of $c_1(\eta)$ (i.e.\ replacing $n_0(|D|)$ by $3n_0(|D|)$) and renaming constants \[ c_1(\eta):=\frac{3(\eta+1)}{\theta}, \qquad c_2(\eta):=C''_{\rm grid}M, \] we obtain \[ n_*(|D|) := \bigl\lceil c_1(\eta)\,\log|D| \bigr\rceil \] Thus we have shown \(\mathbb{P}(\widetilde\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c)\le c_2(\eta)\,|D|^{-\eta}\). Since \(\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c\subseteq \widetilde\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c\), the same bound holds for \(\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)^c)\).
nodes.statement_short: Choose n of order log|D| for a polynomial tail
nodes.section: Margins, single-flip locality, and window envelopes (verifies ass:G1,ass:G3,ass:G2prime)

nodes.name: Fix objects
nodes.statement: Fix $\theta\in\Theta_\circ$ and a deterministic labelling $r$. Let $r^\star$ denote the true labelling on $D$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix theta, r and r*

nodes.name: Intensity formulas
nodes.statement: Under the Hawkes model specification, \begin{align*} \widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta) =& \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta)\,d\widehat N_\ell^r(\tau'),\\ \lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta) =& \mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta)\,d N_\ell(\tau'). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write label-induced and oracle intensities

nodes.name: Oracle equals true-label intensity
nodes.statement: Under the stated conditioning (empty history or marked pre-$t^\ast$ history fixed), the marked past entering the Hawkes functional is the same in $\widehat\lambda^{r^\star}$ and in the oracle intensity, and moreover $\widehat N_\ell^{r^\star}=N_\ell$ on $D$. Therefore $\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}(\tau;\theta)=\lambda_k(\tau\mid\mathcal G_{t-};\theta)$ for a.e.\ $\tau\in D$, hence $\tilde s_\theta(\tau;r^\star)=s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the conditioning, the r*-induced score is the oracle score

nodes.name: Local event count
nodes.statement: Fix $\tau=(t,x)\in D$ and $k\in\{0,1\}$. Because $g_{k\ell}$ is supported on $(0,h]\times \mathcal B_R$, only events in the truncated neighbourhood $(t-h,t)\times B_R(x)$ contribute. On $\Omega_{n_*}(h,R)$ there are at most $n_*(|D|)$ such events.
nodes.statement_short: At most n_* events in the local window

nodes.name: Intensity perturbation
nodes.statement: For any event $\tau_i$ in this neighbourhood, if $r_i=r_i^\star$ then its contribution is the same under $r$ and $r^\star$; if $r_i\neq r_i^\star$, then its contribution changes from the column $r_i^\star$ kernel to the column $r_i$ kernel, and \cref{ass:col-sim} yields a pointwise bound by $\varepsilon_k$. Therefore, \[ \big|\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)-\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}(\tau;\theta)\big| \ \le\ n_*(|D|)\,\varepsilon_k. \]
nodes.statement_short: Each mislabel changes the intensity by at most eps_k

nodes.name: Log bound
nodes.statement: Using $\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)\ge \underline\mu_k$ and $\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}(\tau;\theta)\ge \underline\mu_k$ from \cref{ass:G1}, the mean-value bound $|\log a-\log b|\le |a-b|/\underline\mu_k$ gives \[ \big|\log\widehat\lambda_k^r(\tau;\theta)-\log\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}(\tau;\theta)\big| \ \le\ \frac{n_*(|D|)\varepsilon_k}{\underline\mu_k} \ \le\ \frac{n_*(|D|)\varepsilon_k}{\underline\mu_{\min}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Mean-value bound on log intensities

nodes.name: Score difference
nodes.statement: Finally, \[ \big|\tilde s_\theta(\tau;r)-s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)\big| = \Big|\big(\log\widehat\lambda_1^r-\log\widehat\lambda_0^r\big) -\big(\log\widehat\lambda_1^{r^\star}-\log\widehat\lambda_0^{r^\star}\big)\Big| \le \sum_{k=0}^1\big|\log\widehat\lambda_k^r-\log\widehat\lambda_k^{r^\star}\big|, \] so the claim follows by summing the previous display over $k=0,1$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the log bounds over k

nodes.name: Relative comparability
nodes.statement: We first develop an explicit relative-comparability constant. Under (A1), for every \(\theta\in\Theta_\circ\), every $\tau$ and every $k$ \begin{align*} \lambda_k^\star(\tau) =&\mu_k(\tau;\theta^\star)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta^\star)\,\mathrm{d} N_\ell(\tau')\\ \le& C_{\rm rel}\Bigl(\mu_k(\tau;\theta)+\sum_{\ell=0}^1\int g_{k\ell}(\tau-\tau';\theta)\,\mathrm{d} N_\ell(\tau')\Bigr)\\ =& C_{\rm rel}\lambda_k(\tau;\theta), \end{align*} where \(C_{\rm rel}:= \max\{C_\mu^{\rm rel}, C_g\}\). In particular, \(\lambda^\star(\tau)\le C_{\rm rel}\bigl(\lambda_0(\tau;\theta)+\lambda_1(\tau;\theta)\bigr)\).
nodes.statement_short: lambda* <= C_rel (lambda_0 + lambda_1)

nodes.name: Mean-value bound
nodes.statement: Next, we find a mean-value bound for $s^{\rm or}$ and removal of denominators. Fix $\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_\circ$. Since $s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)=\log\lambda_1(\tau;\theta)-\log\lambda_0(\tau;\theta)$ and $\lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)\ge \nu_->0$, the mean value theorem gives, for each $\tau$, \[ \big|s^{\rm or}_\theta(\tau)-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}(\tau)\big| \le \|\theta-\theta'\|_2\, \sup_{\vartheta\in[\theta,\theta']} \sum_{k=0}^1\frac{\|\nabla_\theta \lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)\|_2}{\lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem for s^or

nodes.name: Remove lambda*
nodes.statement: Multiplying by $\lambda^\star(\tau)$ and using $\lambda^\star\le C_{\rm rel}(\lambda_0+\lambda_1)$ yields \[ \lambda^\star(\tau)\sum_{k=0}^1\frac{\|\nabla_\theta \lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)\|_2}{\lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)} \le C_{\rm rel}\sum_{k=0}^1 \frac{\lambda_0(\tau;\vartheta)+\lambda_1(\tau;\vartheta)}{\lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)}\, \|\nabla_\theta \lambda_k(\tau;\vartheta)\|_2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Use relative comparability

nodes.name: Key reduction
nodes.statement:
By the ratio bounds (A2), for all $k$, \[  rac{\lambda_0+\lambda_1}{\lambda_k} =1+ rac{\lambda_{1-k}}{\lambda_k} \le 1+\max\{C_{m rat},1/c_{m rat}\} =:C_{m mix}. \] Hence, uniformly in $\vartheta\in\Theta_\circ$, \[ \lambda^\star(	au)\sum_{k=0}^1 rac{\|
abla_	heta \lambda_k(	au;\vartheta)\|_2}{\lambda_k(	au;\vartheta)} \le C_{m rel}C_{m mix}\sum_{k=0}^1 \|
abla_	heta \lambda_k(	au;\vartheta)\|_2. \] Therefore,  egin{equation} \int_D  ig|s^{m or}_	heta-s^{m or}_{	heta'} ig|\,\lambda^\star\,d	au \le C_{m rel}C_{m mix}\,\|	heta-	heta'\|_2 \int_D \sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta_\circ}\sum_{k=0}^1\|
abla_	heta \lambda_k(	au;\vartheta)\|_2\,d	au. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Ratio bounds remove denominators (eq. 42)

nodes.name: Linear gradient bound
nodes.statement: We now obtain a linear bound on gradients in terms of local counts. Because $\Theta_\circ$ is compact and the kernel family is truncated-exponential with bounded $w_{k\ell}$, there exist deterministic constants $C_0,C_1<\infty$ (depending only on $\Theta_\circ,h,R,w_\infty$ and the baseline smoothness on $\Theta_\circ$) such that, for all $\vartheta\in\Theta_\circ$ and $\tau=(t,x)$, \begin{equation} \sum_{k=0}^1 \|\nabla_\theta \lambda_k(t,x;\vartheta)\|_2 \le C_0 + C_1\sum_{\ell=0}^1 N_\ell\!\big((t-h,t)\times B_R(x)\big). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Gradients are linear in local counts (eq. 43)

nodes.name: Fubini bound
nodes.statement: We proceed to develop a spatio-temporal Fubini bound for the averaged local counts. Let \[ v_R:=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}\mu(B_R(y))<\infty \] (which equals $\mu(B_R)$ when $\mu$ is Lebesgue measure). Here and below we write $D^+:=(t^\ast-h,T]\times \mathcal S^{+R}$, i.e.\ $D^+=W^+$ with $W=D$. For each $\ell\in\{0,1\}$, \begin{align} \int_{t^\ast}^T\int_{\mathcal{S}} N_\ell\!\big((t-h,t)\times B_R(x)\big)\,\mu(dx)\,dt &= \int_{(t^\ast-h,T)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \Big(\int_{t^\ast}^T \mathbf{1}\{s\in(t-h,t)\}\,dt\Big)\\ \quad& \cdot \Big(\int_S \mathbf{1}\{y\in B_R(x)\}\,\mu(dx)\Big)\,N_\ell(ds,dy) \nonumber\\ &\le \int_{D^+} h\,v_R\,N_\ell(ds,dy) = h\,v_R\,N_\ell(D^+), \end{align} since $\int_{t^\ast}^T \mathbf{1}\{s\in(t-h,t)\}\,dt\le h$ and $\int_S \mathbf{1}\{y\in B_R(x)\}\,\mu(dx)=\mu(\mathcal{S}\cap B_R(y))\le v_R$, and the integrand vanishes outside $D^+$. The same computation with $t$ integrated over $(a,b]$ (instead of $(t^\ast,T]$) yields \[ \int_a^b\int_{\mathcal S} N_\ell((t-h,t)\times B_R(x))\,\mu(dx)\,dt \ \le\ h v_R\,N_\ell(W^+), \qquad W=(a,b]\times\mathcal S, \] so on $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$ we have $N_\ell(W^+)\le K_{\rm act}|W^+|$ uniformly over $W\in\mathcal W_{\rm sch}$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrated local counts are bounded by h v_R N(D^+) (eq. 44)

nodes.name: Combine on E^Lip
nodes.statement: We now conclude (Assumption~\ref{ass:G5}) on $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$. Combine \eqref{eq:key-reduction}, \eqref{eq:grad-linear-fixed} and \eqref{eq:fubini-fixed} to get \[ \int_D \big|s^{\rm or}_\theta-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}\big|\,\lambda^\star\,d\tau \le C_{\rm rel}C_{\rm mix}\,\|\theta-\theta'\|_2 \Big( C_0|D| + C_1 h v_R \sum_{\ell=0}^1 N_\ell(D^+) \Big). \] On $E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|}$ we have $\sum_{\ell=0}^1 N_\ell(D^+)\le K_{\rm act}|D^+|$, hence \[ \int_D \big|s^{\rm or}_\theta-s^{\rm or}_{\theta'}\big|\,\lambda^\star\,d\tau \le C_{\rm rel}C_{\rm mix}\,\|\theta-\theta'\|_2 \Big( C_0|D| + C_1 h v_R K_{\rm act}|D^+| \Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three bounds and the activity event

nodes.name: Define L_s
nodes.statement: Define \[ L_s(|D|) :=C_{\rm rel}C_{\rm mix}\left(C_0 + C_1 h v_R K_{\rm act}\,\frac{|D^+|}{|D|}\right), \] which is deterministic given the window geometry and model constants. Then \eqref{eq:G5-hawkes} follows. Finally, by \eqref{eq:hawkes-activity} we have $\Pr((E^{\rm Lip}_{|D|})^c)\le |D|^{-\eta}$, completing the verification of Assumption~\ref{ass:G5}.
nodes.statement_short: Define L_s(|D|) and conclude

nodes.name: Telescoping path
nodes.statement: Fix $u$ and $\theta\in\Theta_{\rm sc}$. Let $(r^{(j)})_{j=0}^{\mathfrak I}$ be the canonical telescoping path from $r$ to $r^\star$ from \cref{def:telescoping-path}, where $\mathfrak I=d_H^{[u]}(r,r^\star)$ and each adjacent pair differs by a single flip at some index $i_j\le N^{[u]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix u, theta and the canonical telescoping path

nodes.name: Reduce to single flip
nodes.statement:
By the triangle inequality, \[  ig\|
abla f_r^{[u]}(	heta)-
abla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(	heta) ig\| \le \sum_{j=1}^{\mathfrak I}  ig\|
abla f_{r^{(j-1)}}^{[u]}(	heta)-
abla f_{r^{(j)}}^{[u]}(	heta) ig\|. \] It therefore suffices to bound the change in $
abla f^{[u]}$ under a single flip.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality reduces to a single-flip bound

nodes.name: Score formula
nodes.statement:
Fix a single flip at $\gamma_{i}=(t_{i},x_{i})$ and denote the two labellings before/after the flip by $r$ and $r'$. Write $W:=D^{[u]}$ for brevity. By definition, \[ 
abla f_r^{[u]}(	heta) = rac{1}{|W|}\left\{\sum_{j:\,t_j\le u}
abla_	heta\log\widehat\lambda_{r_j}^r(\gamma_j;	heta) -\int_W 
abla_	heta \widehat\lambda^r(	au;	heta)\,d	auight\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write the prefix score for the two labellings

nodes.name: Flipped event term
nodes.statement:
With respect to the event-sum part, at the flipped event $\gamma_i$, predictability implies $\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(\gamma_i;	heta)=\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(\gamma_i;	heta)$ for $k\in\{0,1\}$, so the only change is the component index inside $\log(\cdot)$. Hence \[ \left\|
abla\log\widehat\lambda_{r'_{i}}^{r'}(\gamma_i;	heta) -
abla\log\widehat\lambda_{r_{i}}^{r}(\gamma_i;	heta)ight\| \le 2\max_{k\in\{0,1\}}\|
abla\log\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(\gamma_i;	heta)\| \le 2L_{\log}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Predictability: the flipped event contributes at most 2 L_log

nodes.name: Forward-cone events
nodes.statement:
For any other event $\gamma_j$ with $t_j\le u$, changing the label at $\gamma_{i}$ can only affect $\widehat\lambda_\cdot(\gamma_j;	heta)$ if $\gamma_j\in C_{i}^{[u]}$ (kernel support $(0,L]	imes B_R$). On $C_{i}^{[u]}$, for each $k$,  egin{align*}  ig\|
abla\log\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(	au;	heta)-
abla\log\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(	au;	heta) ig\| &= \left\| rac{
abla\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(	au;	heta)}{\widehat\lambda_k^{r'}(	au;	heta)} - rac{
abla\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(	au;	heta)}{\widehat\lambda_k^{r}(	au;	heta)}ight\|\ &\le  rac{\|\Delta(
abla \widehat\lambda_k^r)(	au;	heta)\|}{\underline\mu_{\min}} + rac{\|
abla \widehat\lambda_k^{r}(	au;	heta)\|}{\underline\mu_{\min}^2}\,|\Delta\widehat\lambda_k^r(	au;	heta)| \ \le\ C_{\log}, \end{align*} by \cref{ass:G1,ass:G3}. Therefore the event-sum contribution is bounded by \[ 2L_{\log}+C_{\log}\,N(C_{i}^{[u]}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Only events in the forward cone change, each by at most C_log

nodes.name: Compensator part
nodes.statement:
With respect to the compensator part, by the $L^1$ gradient influence bound in \cref{ass:G3}, \[ \left\|\int_W 
abla\widehat\lambda^{r'}(	au;	heta)\,d	au - \int_W 
abla\widehat\lambda^{r}(	au;	heta)\,d	auight\| \le \int_W \|\Delta(
abla\widehat\lambda^{r})(	au;	heta)\|\,d	au \le \overline B_1^\Sigma. \]
nodes.statement_short: L1 gradient influence bound

nodes.name: Single-flip bound
nodes.statement: Combining (i) and (ii), \[ \big\|\nabla f_{r'}^{[u]}(\theta)-\nabla f_{r}^{[u]}(\theta)\big\| \le \frac{1}{|W|}\Big(2L_{\log}+C_{\log}N(C_{i}^{[u]})+\overline B_1^\Sigma\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Combine event-sum and compensator parts

nodes.name: Absorb constants
nodes.statement: On $E^{\rm cone}(z_{\rm Fr})$, substitute the bound on $N(C_i^{[u]})$ and use $K_{\rm win}\ge 1$ to absorb $2L_{\log}+\overline B_1^\Sigma$ into the $K_{\rm win}$ term, giving \[ \big\|\nabla f_{r'}^{[u]}(\theta)-\nabla f_{r}^{[u]}(\theta)\big\| \le \frac{1}{|W|}\Big(\bar C_0 K_{\rm win} + \bar C_1\sqrt{K_{\rm win} z_{\rm Fr}} + \bar C_2 z_{\rm Fr}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the cone-count bound

nodes.name: Sum over path
nodes.statement: We now sum over the telescoping path. Summing the single-flip bound over $\mathfrak I=d_H^{[u]}(r,r^\star)$ flips yields the stated inequality for $\|\nabla f_r^{[u]}(\theta)-\nabla f_{r^\star}^{[u]}(\theta)\|$. Uniformity in $\theta$ allows evaluation at $\theta=\hat\theta_r^{[u]}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over the d_H flips

nodes.name: Cone count tail
nodes.statement: Fix $(u,j)$ and consider $C_j^{[u]}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:predictable-cone}, $\mathbf 1_{C_j^{[u]}}$ is $\mathcal G$-predictable, so Freedman inequality applies to \( N(C_j^{[u]})-\int_{C_j^{[u]}}\lambda^\star(\tau)\,d\tau. \) On $\Omega_{n_*}(L,R)$ we have $\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\le K_{\rm win}$, hence $\int_{C_j^{[u]}}\lambda^\star\le K_{\rm win}|C_j^{[u]}|\le V_{L,R}K_{\rm win}$. Therefore \[ \mathbb P\!\left( N(C_j^{[u]})>V_{L,R}K_{\rm win}+\sqrt{2V_{L,R}K_{\rm win}z_{\rm Fr}}+\frac23 z_{\rm Fr},\ \Omega_{n_*}(L,R) \right)\le e^{-z_{\rm Fr}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Cones are predictable, so Freedman bounds the cone counts

nodes.name: Union bound over cones
nodes.statement: On $E_{\rm act}$, the number of cones in the defining intersection of $E^{\rm cone}(z_{\rm Fr})$ is at most $\sum_{m=1}^{\mathfrak{T}} N^{[u_m]}\le \mathfrak{T} N(D)\le (1+\eta_{\rm act})C_{\rm act}|D|\,\mathfrak{T}$, so the union bound yields the displayed probability bound in the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound over cones
